/guides/publish-from-unreal.html:
How-to guides

Publish from Unreal#

Status: verified on Unreal Engine 5.8.3 (Apple silicon), 2026-10-13. The Publish to Verse window was clicked through on a real lit level (the Lumberyard Bistro interior, 1 M triangles, Unreal-native materials, Lightmass lighting): Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse → Publish → upload progress ("Uploading… 31 % (resumable, 8 MB parts)") → the server's compile stages → the link. The click-through is an editor automation test that ships with the plug-in (VersePublish.Window.PublishClickThrough, below). The console command and CI path are verified on the same level.

Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse exports the current level (or the selected actors) to GLB with Epic's bundled glTF Exporter, streams the upload with progress, shows the server's compile stages in the window, and hands back a streaming link.

You need: Unreal Engine 5.3 or newer (verified on 5.8.3) with a C++ toolchain (Visual Studio or Xcode) — or a prebuilt plugin (below) — and the engine's GLTF Exporter plugin (declared as a dependency, normally enabled for you).

1. Install the plugin#

Download#

Download VersePublish-UE5.8-3.0.0.zip (3.0 MB) from the downloads page. It is the source plug-in (the editor compiles it) with verse-prepare for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux under Resources/bin/. Check it before installing:

shasum -a 256 VersePublish-UE5.8-3.0.0.zip   # Windows: Get-FileHash VersePublish-UE5.8-3.0.0.zip -Algorithm SHA256
# 32385ecc8f96b71d04034f940b497a10432e5e680926727881e33c36a5a49ea3

Close the editor and unzip into your project so the descriptor lands at <Project>/Plugins/VersePublish/VersePublish.uplugin (create Plugins/ next to the .uproject if needed).

Building from source instead: cd integrations/unreal/VersePublish && ./make_plugin_zip.sh (→ dist/VersePublish-UE5.8-3.0.0.zip), then unzip it the same way.

Open the project. Let the editor compile the plugin module when prompted; enable the GLTF Exporter plugin if asked and restart.

Blueprint-only projects cannot compile plugin code on open. Build it once against your engine and drop the result in instead:

"<UE>/Engine/Build/BatchFiles/RunUAT.sh" BuildPlugin \
  -Plugin="$PWD/integrations/unreal/VersePublish/VersePublish.uplugin" \
  -Package=/tmp/VersePublish-built -TargetPlatforms=Mac   # Win64 on Windows

Copy /tmp/VersePublish-built (minus HostProject/) to <Project>/Plugins/VersePublish/ and add the verse-prepare binary for your platform under Resources/bin/ (the zip from make_plugin_zip.sh already carries it).

2. Settings#

Project Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ Verse Publish (the window's Settings… button jumps there):

SettingWhat it does
Server URLDefaults to the hosted service. Set your own origin when you run your own server.
Resumable upload above (MB)Default 100. Exports larger than this go through the resumable upload (begin / 8 MB parts / commit): a dropped connection resumes where the server stopped instead of starting over. The window shows "(resumable, 8 MB parts)" next to the percentage.
Account tokenOptional. Sent as Authorization: Bearer; owned scenes are permanent and managed from /studio, and draw from the per-token rate bucket (20/hour). Stored in your per-user EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini, never in shared, source-controlled config.

Setting the Server URL in an .ini by hand? Quote it — ServerUrl="http://localhost:8080" — because // starts a comment in Unreal config files and an unquoted URL is cut to http:. The plugin detects that and says so instead of failing to connect.

3. Publish#

  1. Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse (also a toolbar button).
  2. The scene name defaults to the level name. Tick Selected actors only for a subset.
  3. Press Publish to Verse.

The window shows upload % and then the server's compile stage text verbatim ("Compiling — geometry (41 s)"). Cancel works at any time; the whole publish has a 30-minute budget. On success the URL appears with Copy and Open in Browser and is copied to the clipboard; on failure the server's error text is shown verbatim (quota, limit and auth messages come straight from the app — the X-Verse-Error header is how the plugin tells app errors from edge failures, and only the latter are retried once).

If the server cannot be reached at all, the window says so in plain words ("Could not reach the Verse server at <host>. Check the Server URL …") instead of a transport error.

Publish from a script or CI#

The console command runs the same export → prepare → upload → compile chain without the window:

VersePublish.Publish [scene-name] [server=<url>] [bake=auto|on|off] [quality=draft|high] [resumable=<MB>] [from=<glb>] [strict=1] [wait] [quit]
VersePublish.BakeGlb <in.glb> [out.glb] [high]     # the lighting bake on a saved export

From the Output Log, -ExecCmds, or Python (unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "VersePublish.Publish my-scene wait quit") in a script passed with UnrealEditor-Cmd <project> -ExecutePythonScript=…). wait pumps HTTP until done (needed when the script would otherwise return first); quit exits with status 0 on success, 1 on failure. Each phase is logged under LogVersePublishHeadless and the result is written to Saved/VersePublish/last-publish.json (with uploadBytes, resumable, missingMaterials, keptExport, retry and per-phase timings).

  • A failure never deletes the export. After the export has finished, a failed prepare / upload / compile moves the GLB to Saved/VersePublish/failed/<scene>-<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>.glb (the newest 2 are kept) and logs retry from this export: VersePublish.Publish <scene> from=failed/<file>.glb wait plus the full UnrealEditor-Cmd line. from=<glb> (absolute, or relative to Saved/VersePublish/) publishes that file without re-exporting; one already marked by verse-prepare is uploaded as is.
  • Missing material libraries are checked before the export: packages the level's meshes and materials reference that do not exist (Megascans / Fab content without the Fab plug-in — /Bridge/MSPresets/…, /Fab/Materials/Standard/M_MS_Srf) and material instances whose parent did not load. Each is logged as a warning with the fix (install the Fab plug-in for Unreal 5.8 from the Epic Games Launcher); the window shows the same in yellow. strict=1 refuses to export instead.
  • Invalid numbers. Unreal 5.8's glTF exporter can write inf / nan ("ior":inf), which is not JSON; they are replaced with safe values right after the export (export fix — … ior: inf -> 1.5 in the log).
  • Two Sided Foliage materials (exported by the engine as Default Lit) become double-sided foliage: BLEND → MASK at 0.5, extras.verse.material = "foliage" (two-sided leaf shading with back-lit translucency and wind sway in Verse) and KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission 0.35 for other viewers. The subsurface colour and its per-pixel mask are approximated (white transmission tinted by the base colour).
  • verse-prepare not found (optional — without it the server prepares the export): the log names the exact path to put the binary at (<plugin>/Resources/bin/verse-prepare-darwin-arm64 on Apple silicon) and where to get it. A plug-in built from source in the repo finds target/release/verse-prepare; sh bundle_prepare.sh puts the Mac binaries into Resources/bin before RunUAT BuildPlugin. A window publish logs every phase under LogVersePublishWindow and writes Saved/VersePublish/last-window-publish.json.

Click-through test. The plug-in carries an editor automation test that does what a person does: checks the Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse entry, opens the window, presses Publish to Verse and waits for the link, saving snapshots of the window (Saved/VersePublish/window-*.png):

UnrealEditor <proj> <map> -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests VersePublish.Window.PublishClickThrough;Quit"

The export fixes and the kept export have editor-free tests too:

UnrealEditor-Cmd <proj> -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests VersePublish.GlbFix;Quit" -unattended -nullrhi

Bake materials & lighting (bake-on-publish)#

Unreal materials are graphs, and built (Lightmass) lighting lives in lightmaps that only Unreal's own viewer reads, so a plain glTF export loses the lighting and scenes arrive flat. The window's **Bake materials & lighting** checkbox (and Project Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ Verse Publish ▸ Bake) bakes them in the editor before upload:

Setting
Bake materials & lighting (tri-state: Auto / On / Off)Auto is on for scenes (built lighting present, 6+ static meshes, 2+ lights or ≥ 3 m across) and off for a single product.
High qualityOff (Draft): material bakes up to 1K, lightmap bakes up to 1K per actor at 96 px/m. On (High): material bakes up to 2K, lightmap bakes up to 4K per actor at 256 px/m.

Materials. The engine's glTF exporter renders every non-trivial material input (node graphs, material functions, layers) through the Material Baking module (BakeMaterialInputs = UseMeshData); the bake sets its size from the largest texture in the graph, capped by the quality.

Lighting. The exporter carries each actor's lightmap (EPIC_lightmap_textures). The plug-in then rewrites the GLB: every triangle of a lit actor is rasterised in its lightmap UV space; per texel the base colour (the exporter's baked texture × factor) is multiplied by the lightmap decoded with Unreal's own HQ formula (LightmapCommon.ush — log luminance with the second layer's residual, black point, UVW scale/add) plus emission, then put through the editor's filmic tone curve. The actor is exported with one emissive-only <actor>_Baked material on the lightmap UV set — the shape Verse renders unlit. Movable actors in a baked level get an emissive copy of their material lit by the level's average baked light (never black), the punctual lights are dropped (they are in the bake) and the extension is removed. Only the JSON and the touched accessors/images are read; the binary chunk streams into the new file in 16 MB blocks. Progress and Cancel: Baking lightmaps 12 / 48 (FScopedSlowTask).

Console / CI: VersePublish.Publish <name> bake=auto|on|off quality=draft|high [server=<url>] wait quit; Saved/VersePublish/last-publish.json carries a bake object (lightmaps carried, materials made, textures, ambient-lit, lights removed, seconds).

Exposure and tone. The bake applies what the viewport applies: the level's exposure (an unbound post-process volume with manual exposure is reproduced exactly; auto exposure is estimated from the baked light — middle grey on the log-average) and Unreal's own tone mapper (the filmic curve in ACEScg with gamut expansion and blue correction). Metals keep only a dim share of their base colour (Unreal gives them no diffuse light; their reflections cannot be baked). A level whose lights are all Movable has empty lightmaps: the plug-in then leaves the lighting live instead of baking a black scene. Lightmaps leave the engine's glTF exporter gamma-encoded (its canvas renders at gamma 2.2); the bake decodes that.

Building lighting on macOS (Apple silicon). Lightmass works — a Preview build of the 1 M-triangle Bistro interior with 11 static lights takes about 15 s — once two things are true:

  1. ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1 is in the editor's environment. UnrealLightmass on Mac ships as an x86_64 binary and runs under Rosetta 2, which does not advertise AVX by default; Embree then fails to create its device and Lightmass dies with Assertion failed: rtcGetDeviceError(EmbreeDevice) == RTC_ERROR_NONE (Engine/Programs/UnrealLightmass/Saved/Logs, or ~/Library/Logs/Unreal Engine/UnrealLightmass). The editor only says "Lighting build failed". Start the editor from a shell with the variable set (ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1 open -a UnrealEditor does not pass it — launch the binary .../UnrealEditor.app/Contents/MacOS/UnrealEditor directly, or set it with launchctl setenv ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX 1 before opening the editor).
  2. **The build runs in a ticking editor with no other Unreal editor open.** There is no Swarm Agent on Mac: the editor and Lightmass pair over UDP messaging (SwarmInterfaceLocal.cpp) and Lightmass takes the first editor that answers its ping. A second open editor can take the job; a commandlet (-run=resavepackages -buildlighting) never answers (its game thread is blocked) and Lightmass gives up with "Timed out waiting for the recipient". A Wi-Fi network change during a build also lost the pairing once — rebuild.

integrations/bake-proof/unreal_build_lighting.py builds a map from a script this way; integrations/bake-proof/unreal_bistro_level.py builds the whole proof level (import, materials, lights, Lightmass).

Measured (2026-10-13, UE 5.8.3, M5 Pro). The Bistro interior (OBJ → GLB, 66 meshes, 1 M triangles), dressed in Unreal-native materials — a master material with parameters calling a material function (MF_Grime), 14 material instances of it, a layered material (brass / iron attribute layers blended by a mask) and a procedural tile floor — lit by 11 static point lights at the model's own lamps (Lightmass Preview, lightmaps 32–256). Editor frame vs the published link at the editor camera, CIEDE2000 mean over the frame (compare.mjs, black backdrop like the editor's):

bake offDraftHigh
ΔE2000 mean / median45.5 / 46.817.9 / 16.719.1 / 14.1
SSIM0.020.570.58
publish, click to link26 s36 s (1.4×)123 s
bake step—5.6 s63 s

Bake off arrives flat and, on this level, through the compatibility fallback (the streamed compile rejected the export's light nodes as out of bounds), so it does not frame like the editor at all. The remaining gap with the bake on is mostly the viewer's own finishing (it re-exposes a baked scene to a median of 0.40 and adds its post effects) and the tone mapper's red handling (Unreal's RRT red modifier and glow are not reproduced); the target of ΔE ≤ 15 is met on the median for High, not on the mean.

Limits. Directionality is approximated (Unreal's non-directional 0.6 factor); stationary/movable lights' direct light is not in a lightmap and therefore not in the bake. Translucent and masked primitives keep their live material. Without built lighting the bake only raises the material bake size.

The prepare step (2.3)#

Between export and upload the plug-in runs verse-prepare on the GLB: textures are right-sized to the texel density the scene can show (default 2048 px/m — one texel per screen pixel at arm's length), opaque base colour goes to JPEG 92 (everything else stays lossless), duplicate meshes are instanced and unreferenced data is dropped. The panel shows the tool's own progress and result. Prepared files may be up to 20 GB; without the tool, exports upload as they are up to the plan's raw upload limit (the server prepares them) and the log carries the install hint. Preferences: prepare on/off, the binary path, texels per metre, lossless. Details, flags and how the binaries are bundled: verse-prepare.

What gets exported#

GLB with embedded textures at source resolution — nothing is downscaled or recompressed. The Verse pipeline preserves up to 4K per material on its hero tier, and base colour above 4K (8K, 16K) at full detail through virtual texturing, so bake lightmaps at the quality you want published; downscaling before upload permanently caps the result.

Known issues with Unreal exports (October 2026)#

Found reviewing a large Unreal exterior against Unreal's own renders of the same cameras. Where Verse now corrects for the exporter it says so; the rest are open.

  • Sun direction: under investigation, not fixed. The export's directional light (the level's Unreal Sun) arrives as engine azimuth 101.1°, elevation 25.6°. On the review cameras, Unreal's rendered shadows match azimuth 281°: the same elevation, the opposite side of the sky. Whether the sign is lost in the glTF exporter or in how Verse reads the light is not yet known. Until it is, check the shadows on the link against the editor and set the sun on the link (?sun=) or in the Sun panel (and save the look) if they disagree.
  • Ultra Dynamic Sky drives the sun at runtime. Its Blueprint sets the sun's direction, colour and intensity when the game runs, so the directional light the exporter sees is the editor-time actor and need not match what Unreal renders. Its sky dome is exported as a mesh (reported as "sky dome"); Verse draws its own sky.
  • Unset materials arrive as rough metal. Where the exporter does not write a material's surface (graph-driven plaster, slate, travertine, wood, concrete, fabric), it leaves glTF's defaults, metallic 1 / roughness 1, which renders dark. The compiler in the next release (not yet on production) reads exactly (1, 1) with no metallic-roughness texture as a non-metal, unless the material's name contains a metal word (metal, steel, chrome, silver, gold, bronze, brass, copper, aluminium, iron, nickel, titanium): name real metals accordingly. Leaves and walls exported with metallic factor 1 and the real ~0 in the texture are handled on staging by folding in the texture's mean.
  • Graph-driven roughness is lost. A roughness computed in the material graph can be exported as a bare factor: one scene's pavers arrived at roughness 0.1 (a mirror of the sky) and its asphalt at 50 % metal. This is not detected. Fix it in Unreal with a plain roughness/metallic input, or patch the compiled scene with verse-matfix --surface PREFIX=rough,metal (an operator tool).
  • Translucent glass arrives OPAQUE. The exporter drops a Translucent material's blend mode. On staging, an opaque material whose name says glass or glazing (whole word) is drawn as glass with 0.8 transmission; other translucent materials need a glass name or KHR_materials_transmission.
  • Baked re-exports carry no lights. A level exported with baked lighting has no KHR_lights_punctual, so the scene falls back to the default sun. Set the sun on the link, or (operators) copy the directional lights of an unbaked export of the same level into the scene's stage with the stage-sun tool in the repository's tools/ folder.

Known seams to watch#

  • GLTFExporter API drift (UGLTFExporter::ExportToGLTF, UGLTFExportOptions, the lightmap canvas gamma) — unchanged through 5.8.
  • The 5.3 vs 5.4 progress-delegate split.
  • Lightmass on Apple silicon needs ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1 (above).

Next#

  • Share privately with tokens
  • Embed the viewer
  • Publish from Unity

The subsurface colour and its per-pixel mask are approximated (white transmission tinted by the base colour).

A plug-in built from source in the repo finds target/release/verse-prepare; sh bundle_prepare.sh puts the Mac binaries into Resources/bin before RunUAT BuildPlugin. A window publish logs every phase under LogVersePublishWindow and writes Saved/VersePublish/last-window-publish.json.

Click-through test. The plug-in carries an editor automation test that does what a person does: checks the Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse entry, opens the window, presses Publish to Verse and waits for the link, saving snapshots of the window (Saved/VersePublish/window-*.png):

Copy
UnrealEditor <proj> <map> -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests VersePublish.Window.PublishClickThrough;Quit"

The export fixes and the kept export have editor-free tests too:

Copy
UnrealEditor-Cmd <proj> -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests VersePublish.GlbFix;Quit" -unattended -nullrhi
Bake materials & lighting (bake-on-publish)#

Unreal materials are graphs, and built (Lightmass) lighting lives in lightmaps that only Unreal's own viewer reads, so a plain glTF export loses the lighting and scenes arrive flat. The window's **Bake materials & lighting** checkbox (and Project Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ Verse Publish ▸ Bake) bakes them in the editor before upload:

Setting	
Bake materials & lighting (tri-state: Auto / On / Off)	Auto is on for scenes (built lighting present, 6+ static meshes, 2+ lights or ≥ 3 m across) and off for a single product.
High quality	Off (Draft): material bakes up to 1K, lightmap bakes up to 1K per actor at 96 px/m. On (High): material bakes up to 2K, lightmap bakes up to 4K per actor at 256 px/m.

Materials. The engine's glTF exporter renders every non-trivial material input (node graphs, material functions, layers) through the Material Baking module (BakeMaterialInputs = UseMeshData); the bake sets its size from the largest texture in the graph, capped by the quality.

Lighting. The exporter carries each actor's lightmap (EPIC_lightmap_textures). The plug-in then rewrites the GLB: every triangle of a lit actor is rasterised in its lightmap UV space; per texel the base colour (the exporter's baked texture × factor) is multiplied by the lightmap decoded with Unreal's own HQ formula (LightmapCommon.ush — log luminance with the second layer's residual, black point, UVW scale/add) plus emission, then put through the editor's filmic tone curve. The actor is exported with one emissive-only <actor>_Baked material on the lightmap UV set — the shape Verse renders unlit. Movable actors in a baked level get an emissive copy of their material lit by the level's average baked light (never black), the punctual lights are dropped (they are in the bake) and the extension is removed. Only the JSON and the touched accessors/images are read; the binary chunk streams into the new file in 16 MB blocks. Progress and Cancel: Baking lightmaps 12 / 48 (FScopedSlowTask).

Console / CI: VersePublish.Publish <name> bake=auto|on|off quality=draft|high [server=<url>] wait quit; Saved/VersePublish/last-publish.json carries a bake object (lightmaps carried, materials made, textures, ambient-lit, lights removed, seconds).

Exposure and tone. The bake applies what the viewport applies: the level's exposure (an unbound post-process volume with manual exposure is reproduced exactly; auto exposure is estimated from the baked light — middle grey on the log-average) and Unreal's own tone mapper (the filmic curve in ACEScg with gamut expansion and blue correction). Metals keep only a dim share of their base colour (Unreal gives them no diffuse light; their reflections cannot be baked). A level whose lights are all Movable has empty lightmaps: the plug-in then leaves the lighting live instead of baking a black scene. Lightmaps leave the engine's glTF exporter gamma-encoded (its canvas renders at gamma 2.2); the bake decodes that.

Building lighting on macOS (Apple silicon). Lightmass works — a Preview build of the 1 M-triangle Bistro interior with 11 static lights takes about 15 s — once two things are true:

ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1 is in the editor's environment. UnrealLightmass on Mac ships as an x86_64 binary and runs under Rosetta 2, which does not advertise AVX by default; Embree then fails to create its device and Lightmass dies with Assertion failed: rtcGetDeviceError(EmbreeDevice) == RTC_ERROR_NONE (Engine/Programs/UnrealLightmass/Saved/Logs, or ~/Library/Logs/Unreal Engine/UnrealLightmass). The editor only says "Lighting build failed". Start the editor from a shell with the variable set (ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1 open -a UnrealEditor does not pass it — launch the binary .../UnrealEditor.app/Contents/MacOS/UnrealEditor directly, or set it with launchctl setenv ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX 1 before opening the editor).
**The build runs in a ticking editor with no other Unreal editor open.** There is no Swarm Agent on Mac: the editor and Lightmass pair over UDP messaging (SwarmInterfaceLocal.cpp) and Lightmass takes the first editor that answers its ping. A second open editor can take the job; a commandlet (-run=resavepackages -buildlighting) never answers (its game thread is blocked) and Lightmass gives up with "Timed out waiting for the recipient". A Wi-Fi network change during a build also lost the pairing once — rebuild.

integrations/bake-proof/unreal_build_lighting.py builds a map from a script this way; integrations/bake-proof/unreal_bistro_level.py builds the whole proof level (import, materials, lights, Lightmass).

Measured (2026-10-13, UE 5.8.3, M5 Pro). The Bistro interior (OBJ → GLB, 66 meshes, 1 M triangles), dressed in Unreal-native materials — a master material with parameters calling a material function (MF_Grime), 14 material instances of it, a layered material (brass / iron attribute layers blended by a mask) and a procedural tile floor — lit by 11 static point lights at the model's own lamps (Lightmass Preview, lightmaps 32–256). Editor frame vs the published link at the editor camera, CIEDE2000 mean over the frame (compare.mjs, black backdrop like the editor's):

	bake off	Draft	High
ΔE2000 mean / median	45.5 / 46.8	17.9 / 16.7	19.1 / 14.1
SSIM	0.02	0.57	0.58
publish, click to link	26 s	36 s (1.4×)	123 s
bake step	—	5.6 s	63 s

Bake off arrives flat and, on this level, through the compatibility fallback (the streamed compile rejected the export's light nodes as out of bounds), so it does not frame like the editor at all. The remaining gap with the bake on is mostly the viewer's own finishing (it re-exposes a baked scene to a median of 0.40 and adds its post effects) and the tone mapper's red handling (Unreal's RRT red modifier and glow are not reproduced); the target of ΔE ≤ 15 is met on the median for High, not on the mean.

Limits. Directionality is approximated (Unreal's non-directional 0.6 factor); stationary/movable lights' direct light is not in a lightmap and therefore not in the bake. Translucent and masked primitives keep their live material. Without built lighting the bake only raises the material bake size.

The prepare step (2.3)#

Between export and upload the plug-in runs verse-prepare on the GLB: textures are right-sized to the texel density the scene can show (default 2048 px/m — one texel per screen pixel at arm's length), opaque base colour goes to JPEG 92 (everything else stays lossless), duplicate meshes are instanced and unreferenced data is dropped. The panel shows the tool's own progress and result. Prepared files may be up to 20 GB; without the tool, exports upload as they are up to the plan's raw upload limit (the server prepares them) and the log carries the install hint. Preferences: prepare on/off, the binary path, texels per metre, lossless. Details, flags and how the binaries are bundled: verse-prepare.

What gets exported#

GLB with embedded textures at source resolution — nothing is downscaled or recompressed. The Verse pipeline preserves up to 4K per material on its hero tier, and base colour above 4K (8K, 16K) at full detail through virtual texturing, so bake lightmaps at the quality you want published; downscaling before upload permanently caps the result.

Known issues with Unreal exports (October 2026)#

Found reviewing a large Unreal exterior against Unreal's own renders of the same cameras. Where Verse now corrects for the exporter it says so; the rest are open.

Sun direction: under investigation, not fixed. The export's directional light (the level's Unreal Sun) arrives as engine azimuth 101.1°, elevation 25.6°. On the review cameras, Unreal's rendered shadows match azimuth 281°: the same elevation, the opposite side of the sky. Whether the sign is lost in the glTF exporter or in how Verse reads the light is not yet known. Until it is, check the shadows on the link against the editor and set the sun on the link (?sun=) or in the Sun panel (and save the look) if they disagree.
Ultra Dynamic Sky drives the sun at runtime. Its Blueprint sets the sun's direction, colour and intensity when the game runs, so the directional light the exporter sees is the editor-time actor and need not match what Unreal renders. Its sky dome is exported as a mesh (reported as "sky dome"); Verse draws its own sky.
Unset materials arrive as rough metal. Where the exporter does not write a material's surface (graph-driven plaster, slate, travertine, wood, concrete, fabric), it leaves glTF's defaults, metallic 1 / roughness 1, which renders dark. The compiler in the next release (not yet on production) reads exactly (1, 1) with no metallic-roughness texture as a non-metal, unless the material's name contains a metal word (metal, steel, chrome, silver, gold, bronze, brass, copper, aluminium, iron, nickel, titanium): name real metals accordingly. Leaves and walls exported with metallic factor 1 and the real ~0 in the texture are handled on staging by folding in the texture's mean.
Graph-driven roughness is lost. A roughness computed in the material graph can be exported as a bare factor: one scene's pavers arrived at roughness 0.1 (a mirror of the sky) and its asphalt at 50 % metal. This is not detected. Fix it in Unreal with a plain roughness/metallic input, or patch the compiled scene with verse-matfix --surface PREFIX=rough,metal (an operator tool).
Translucent glass arrives OPAQUE. The exporter drops a Translucent material's blend mode. On staging, an opaque material whose name says glass or glazing (whole word) is drawn as glass with 0.8 transmission; other translucent materials need a glass name or KHR_materials_transmission.
Baked re-exports carry no lights. A level exported with baked lighting has no KHR_lights_punctual, so the scene falls back to the default sun. Set the sun on the link, or (operators) copy the directional lights of an unbaked export of the same level into the scene's stage with the stage-sun tool in the repository's tools/ folder.
Known seams to watch#
GLTFExporter API drift (UGLTFExporter::ExportToGLTF, UGLTFExportOptions, the lightmap canvas gamma) — unchanged through 5.8.
The 5.3 vs 5.4 progress-delegate split.
Lightmass on Apple silicon needs ROSETTA_ADVERTISE_AVX=1 (above).

/guides/share-privately.html:
How-to guides

Share privately with tokens#

By default a published scene is unlisted: anyone with the URL can open it, and it is listed nowhere. For a client review, a pre-launch project or a paying customer you often want more — a scene that only the people you chose can open, and the ability to cut one of them off later without touching the others. That is what private scenes and share tokens do.

You need: an account (free; the token is your credential) and a scene you own. Every call below was run against a live server; HOST is your Verse origin and TOKEN your account token.

1. Get an account and own the scene#

Create the account once. The token is returned once — store it like an API key:

curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/account \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"Studio North"}'
# → {"accountId":"acct-5fab29f5aa8e","name":"Studio North","createdAt":…,
#    "token":"<64 hex, shown once>", "note":"This token is shown once and IS your credential …"}

Scenes you upload with the token are owned automatically — send Authorization: Bearer TOKEN on the ingest (the Blender, Unity and Unreal exporters do this when a token is set in their preferences). An existing anonymous scene can be claimed by id:

curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/scenes/docs-demo-718035483f84/claim \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# → {"id":"docs-demo-718035483f84","owner":"acct-5fab29f5aa8e"}

Owned scenes are permanent (never evicted by the disk budget) and show up in /studio and GET /v1/account/scenes.

2. Make it private#

curl -sS -X PATCH https://HOST/v1/scenes/docs-demo-718035483f84 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"visibility":"private"}'
# → {"id":"docs-demo-718035483f84","visibility":"private"}

From now on every artifact of the scene — the .vpk, its .stage.json and .plan.svg sidecars, its poster — answers 404 to anyone without access. The body is byte-identical to a missing file's, so existence is never advertised; the only tell is an X-Verse-Private: 1 header, which the viewer app uses to say "This scene is private" instead of "expired":

curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://HOST/ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk
# HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
# X-Verse-Private: 1

You still see it yourself, with the Bearer token or the /studio session cookie.

3. Mint a share token per recipient#

curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/scenes/docs-demo-718035483f84/share \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# → {"id":"0ca2f454","suffix":"629b","created":…,"shareToken":"<32 hex, shown once>"}

Mint one per person (up to 32 per scene). The 32-hex shareToken is shown once and stored only as a SHA-256 hash; id is what you revoke by, and suffix is the last four characters so you can tell links apart in a list.

The link you send is the normal share link plus the token:

https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk&share=<shareToken>

The app threads ?share= onto every artifact fetch, including the render worker's byte-range requests, so the recipient streams normally:

curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "Range: bytes=0-1023" \
  "https://HOST/ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk?share=<shareToken>"
# HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
# Cache-Control: private, no-store

Programmatic clients can send X-Verse-Share: <shareToken> instead of the query parameter. In an embed, pass it as the share option — see Embed the viewer.

4. See who has access, and revoke#

curl -sS https://HOST/v1/scenes/docs-demo-718035483f84/share -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# → {"scene":"docs-demo-718035483f84","shares":[{"id":"0ca2f454","suffix":"629b","created":…}]}

curl -sS -X DELETE https://HOST/v1/scenes/docs-demo-718035483f84/share/0ca2f454 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# → {"revoked":"0ca2f454"}

A revoked holder gets plain 404s from the next request on. Other recipients are unaffected. Deleting the scene, or losing ownership, kills every token at once.

/studio does all of this per scene card: a visibility selector plus create / copy / revoke for each share link, listed by suffix.

What private scenes give up#

  • No CDN. With VERSE_CDN_BASE set, public and unlisted scenes redirect to the edge; a private scene never does — CDN copies are public bytes with no auth in front. Remote reviewers of a private scene pay origin round trips by design. Flipping an already-viewed public scene private does not purge an edge's copy; purge it there if the bytes must disappear (an operator topic; ask your Verse contact).
  • Review comments follow the same gate. A private scene's pinned comments are readable and postable only with the owner's auth or a share token — see Collect client review comments.

Reference#

  • Accounts & Studio and Visibility & share tokens in the API reference.
Source: docs/guides/share-privately.md · rendered in the browser from the repository's Markdown.

/guides/floor-plan-to-3d.html:
How-to guides

Floor plan to 3D home#

Upload the floor plan from a project brochure and get a furnished 3D home in about a minute. Buyers can walk through it on their phone, and you can share it on WhatsApp.

You need: the plan as a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF. A screenshot of the brochure page is fine. Any hints you add (carpet area, BHK) make it more accurate.

Make one#

  1. Open the app (/app) and press Floor plan → 3D on the upload screen.
  2. Pick the plan image. Optionally add:
    • Carpet area (sq ft): the most useful hint, because it sets the scale. Built-up and super built-up areas work too; say which one it is.
    • Plan width (m): the outside width of the flat, if you know it. This wins over the area.
    • BHK: caps how many rooms are called bedrooms.
    • Style: Modern Indian, Scandinavian, Luxury or Minimal. This sets the floors, wall paint, wood and fabrics.
    • City and Name: used for the title and the share message.
  3. Press Read plan. After a few seconds the plan comes back as a drawing, with each room coloured by type, its name and its area.
  4. Check it:
    • Tap a room to rename it or change its type (Bedroom, Kitchen, Pooja room…).
    • Rotate 90° or Flip if the plan was read sideways or mirrored. The entrance door is drawn in green, with a green IN marker.
    • Doors. Doors the reader added (the plan didn't show them) are highlighted in orange. Press Edit doors and tap a wall to add a 0.9 m door. Tap a door, window or open gap to switch it between the three, remove it or make it the entrance. Tap IN, then a door or an outside wall, to move the entrance. Every change re-checks that each room can be reached and names the ones that can't. **Add doors for me** adds the fewest doors that connect them. With the keyboard, openings and the IN marker are buttons. In Edit doors a room's panel lists + Door to … for each neighbouring room.
  5. Press Generate 3D home. When it is ready you get the link, an Open button, Share on WhatsApp and Copy link.

The link opens standing at the entrance of the living room. There is one hotspot per room with its name and area, and a short guided tour through the rooms.

What it builds#

  • Walls at 3 m with real openings. Doors are 2.1 m high and drawn open, so you can walk through. Windows run from a 0.9 m sill to 2.1 m and have frames and glass.
  • Floors, ceilings and skirting. Floor materials follow the room type: tiles in bathrooms and the kitchen, outdoor tiles on balconies, wood or marble elsewhere, depending on the style.
  • One ceiling light per room.

  • Furniture by room type:

    RoomFurniture
    Livingsofa, coffee table, TV unit, rug
    Bedroombed, side tables, wardrobe
    Kitchencounter, fridge
    Diningtable, chairs
    BathroomWC, vanity, shower
    Studydesk, chair
    Poojamandir unit
    Balconychairs, table
    Utilitywashing machine
    Foyershoe rack

    Furniture stands against a wall. It stays out of door swings and keeps a 0.75 m walkway, and no two pieces overlap. A piece that does not fit is left out; nothing is squeezed in.

  • Before publishing, the generator walks the home on a 10 cm grid, starting at the entrance. If any room cannot be reached, it does not publish. Instead it names the room, and the plan editor highlights it (usually a door that was read as a window, or a wall that was read through a doorway).

How well it reads plans#

Two readers are used:

  • The plan reader always runs. It needs no AI and no network. It finds the walls (solid, grey or hatched), the gaps in them, and the rooms between them. A gap whose lines run along it is a window; a gap with a drawn door leaf is a door. Measured on the test set (6 flats from 1 to 4 BHK, each drawn in 3 brochure styles — clean, tinted with furniture, and a noisy hatched scan):

    MeasuredTarget
    Wall overlap (IoU)0.86≥ 0.85
    Rooms found95 %≥ 90 %
    Doors92 %≥ 85 %
    Windows94 %≥ 85 %
    Scale error, no hints2.4 %≤ 5 %
    Room types, no AI67 %≥ 60 %

    The reader cannot read text, so it guesses room types from size and layout. For example, the biggest room the entrance opens into is the living room, and small closed rooms are toilets.

  • The AI reader runs only when the operator has turned it on (see below). It reads the labels printed on the plan ("M. BED", "TOI", "KIT", "POOJA"), the dimension text (feet-and-inches or metres) and the entrance. Where the plan reader's rooms agree with the AI's, the plan reader's geometry is kept and the AI supplies names and types. Where they disagree (photos, colour-filled brochures, line drawings), the plan is built from the AI's rooms. The scale comes from the printed room dimensions, measured against the room outlines in pixels.

    Measured with the real Anthropic API (claude-haiku-5-5, the default) on 28 plans. 18 are the synthetic test plans above. 10 are brochure-style plans made for the test: a colour brochure, a tinted plan with wood floors and a watermark, a line drawing, a "SAMPLE FLAT" watermark, a low-resolution plan in metres, a large 4 BHK, two phone photos of the printed page (turned 4° and 7°, keystoned, uneven light), a turned noisy scan, and a two-unit page. These are rooms found, room types right, doors, windows, wall overlap and scale error:

    PlansReaderRoomsTypesDoorsWindowsWallsScale error
    Synthetic, clean (6)Plan reader96 %71 %94 %100 %0.882 %
    AI only100 %100 %74 %66 %0.682 %
    Both99 %100 %94 %100 %0.87< 0.5 %
    Synthetic, tinted (6)Plan reader96 %71 %94 %100 %0.852 %
    AI only100 %100 %96 %98 %0.771 %
    Both99 %100 %94 %100 %0.881 %
    Synthetic, scan (6)Plan reader94 %59 %88 %83 %0.833 %
    AI only100 %100 %59 %55 %0.721 %
    Both99 %100 %88 %90 %0.811 %
    Brochure-style (10)Plan reader49 %29 %51 %46 %0.35152 %
    AI only100 %100 %67 %66 %0.561 %
    Both99 %100 %94 %93 %0.561 %
    All 28Plan reader79 %53 %77 %77 %0.6856 %
    AI only100 %100 %73 %71 %0.661 %
    Both99 %100 %93 %96 %0.751 %

    Per brochure-style plan, with both readers: every plan has 91–100 % of its rooms and 100 % of its types, and every one builds (the walk reaches every room). The weak spots are the phone photos (77–93 % of the doors, 78–83 % of the windows). The plan reader alone cannot read the line drawing, the metric plan, the wood-floor plan or the two photos at all.

    Doors the readers miss. A missed door leaves a room nobody can walk into, and the build refuses the plan. So before the plan is shown, the reader checks it the way the build does and adds the most likely door for every room that can't be reached: on a wall the room shares with a room you can reach, chosen by what the two rooms are (a toilet opens off the passage or a bedroom, not the living room or the kitchen; a pooja room off the living room or the foyer; one attached toilet per bedroom), at a standard width (0.75 m toilet, 0.8 m kitchen, 0.9 m bedroom, 1.2 m balcony), where the AI marked a door if it marked one near there. Floor plan to 3D home#

Upload the floor plan from a project brochure and get a furnished 3D home in about a minute. Buyers can walk through it on their phone, and you can share it on WhatsApp.

Pick the plan image. Optionally add:

Plan width (m): the outside width of the flat, if you know it. This wins over the area.
BHK: caps how many rooms are called bedrooms.
Style: Modern Indian, Scandinavian, Luxury or Minimal. This sets the floors, wall paint, wood and fabrics.
City and Name: used for the title and the share message.
Press Read plan. After a few seconds the plan comes back as a drawing, with each room coloured by type, its name and its area.
Check it:
Tap a room to rename it or change its type (Bedroom, Kitchen, Pooja room…).

Walls at 3 m with real openings. Doors are 2.1 m high and drawn open, so you can walk through. Windows run from a 0.9 m sill to 2.1 m and have frames and glass.

Foyer	shoe rack

Doors	92 %	≥ 85 %

/guides/instant-home.html:
How-to guides

Verse Home: a brochure plan to a home buyers walk, restyle and tour together#

You have the floor plan from a project brochure. A minute later you have a furnished home that walks like a real one. It opens on any phone from a WhatsApp link, changes style while people watch, and a group of buyers can tour it together from one link.

Verse Home combines three features: Floor plan to 3D home, Restyle a space, live and Tour together, live.

The flow#

  1. Upload the plan. Open the upload screen, choose Floor plan → 3D and drop the plan as a PNG, JPG, WebP or PDF. The plan can be a clean export, a tinted brochure page or a phone scan. Add the carpet area and the BHK if you know them. Both make the scale and the room types more reliable.
  2. Check the plan, then Generate. The plan comes back as a drawing. Tap a room to rename it or change its type, and rotate or flip the plan if needed. Doors we added because the plan didn't show them are highlighted in orange ("We added 2 doors — check them"). To change doors, press Edit doors and tap a wall to add a 0.9 m door there. Tap any door, window or open gap to switch it between the three, remove it or make it the entrance. Tap the green IN marker, then a door or an outside wall, to move the entrance. The line above the plan re-checks after every change and names any room that cannot be reached from the entrance. Add doors for me puts in the fewest doors that connect them. A room that still cannot be reached is not published.
  3. Share. The result shows the link, Copy and **Share on WhatsApp**. The link opens walking at the living-room entrance, with a pin for each room.
  4. Restyle. Anyone who opens the link can use the Restyle chip (Original, Scandinavian, Japandi, Luxury Marble, Indian Contemporary, Industrial, Coastal, or plain words such as marble floor). The floors, walls, ceilings, skirting, counters, joinery and fabrics change in place.
  5. Tour together. Tap Tour together on the link and send the invite. Buyers follow your camera from their phones, and when you restyle, everyone in the tour sees the change.

What a generated home is made of#

  • The shell. Walls are 3 m high with real door and window openings. Doors have architraves and panelled leaves and are drawn open. A single leaf hangs on the jamb nearer the room's corner, so it opens back against the side wall. A WC-sized bathroom's door opens out. Windows have frames, glass, a stone sill and architraves. Living and dining rooms get a false-ceiling border with a warm LED cove. Other rooms get a slim cornice, and every room has recessed downlights and its own floor, ceiling and skirting.
  • Furniture, placed the way a stylist would. In the living room the sofa sits on the longest solid wall with a rug under its front legs, a coffee table centred on the rug, a side table and lamp at one end and a floor lamp at the other. The TV unit faces the sofa on a slatted-wood or stone feature wall, with the TV mounted above it. Dining tables are centred under a pendant. Beds go against the longest wall without a window, with nightstands and lamps on both sides, a rug, and art at eye height above the headboard. Each bedroom has a wardrobe, and corners get plants and lounge chairs. Kitchens get a counter run with a sink and tap, a hob, a chimney hood, wall cabinets (never over a window), a backsplash and a fridge. Bathrooms get a WC, a vanity with a lit mirror and a shower. A glass enclosure (0.75–0.9 m) goes in where it fits. In a small WC the shower is a wet-room one: a rain head, a mixer and a floor drain on the open floor. A door that swings out of a small bathroom keeps only a 0.55 m approach inside it, not a full swing square. Living rooms, bedrooms, dining rooms and studies get curtains. The rules stay as before: door-swing keep-outs, 0.75 m walkways, no overlaps and every room reachable on foot. The premium checks add two more: nothing floats, and every wall piece hangs on a wall.
  • Light. The generator bakes the light into the vertex colours with real rays (plan2home-bake.mjs, makeRayBaker): 40 cosine-weighted rays per vertex against the walls, furniture and floor and ceiling planes give soft contact shadows and ambient occlusion (corners, skirting, under a sofa, behind a bed). Rays that leave the flat through a window bring in daylight, and each room's lamps add warm pools. The occluder for a pack model is the model as drawn, not its furniture slot, and the shadow never goes below half brightness. A phone and a desktop render the same light without real-time GI, so the link opens with the studio fill (gi=0;env=1.25;ev=0.35). The bake takes 1–3 s of the build.
  • Surfaces. You have the floor plan from a project brochure. A minute later you have a furnished home that walks like a real one. It opens on any phone from a WhatsApp link, changes style while people watch, and a group of buyers can tour it together from one link.

Reference

Developers: embed, automate, get notified#

Everything a developer needs to put Verse scenes in their own product, in copy-paste form:

  1. <verse-viewer> — one tag on any page.
  2. React and Vue — thin typed wrappers over that tag.
  3. The REST SDK — upload, wait, publish, private links, embed code, analytics.
  4. Webhooks — scene.ready / scene.failed, signed and retried.
  5. MCP server (unreleased) — let AI assistants and agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) upload a 3D file and hand back a Verse link.

Start at the developer hub: a live demo with copy-paste code for HTML, React, Vue, Node and curl, and a playground where you paste a GLB link or drop a small file and get a live preview, the embed code and an SDK snippet. Runnable examples (Next.js, Vite + React, Vue, plain HTML, a Shopify product page, a Node upload script and a webhook receiver) live in sdk/public-examples/; designer tools (Framer, Webflow, Figma) in integrations/designers/ (guide).

Install: npm install @ctruhtech/verse-sdk @ctruhtech/verse-viewer @ctruhtech/verse-react @ctruhtech/verse-vue (take what you need). Each package has a 60-second quickstart in its README.

Replace https://verse.ctruh.com with your Verse origin if you run your own. The account token is the credential — create one in Studio (/studio) or with POST /v1/account; keep it server-side.

Reference: api.md (every route), sdk.md (every SDK method), embed-sdk.md (every viewer verb and event). Postman: web/playground/verse-api.postman_collection.json.

Adoption numbers#

/developers/adoption is a public page of aggregate counts, fed by GET /v1/adoption (JSON, cached five minutes): weekly npm downloads for @ctruhtech/* and the SDK repository's GitHub stars (both fetched by the server and cached an hour), and from the server itself: API keys used in the last 30 days (a count), distinct sites embedding Verse, scenes served per week, and MCP calls. No personal data: a site is kept only as a salted one-way hash, so there is no list, no IP address and no page path.

  • Being listed. A scene owner can opt in with POST /v1/adoption/optin {"listDomains": true} (Bearer token); the sites that embed their scenes are then named on the page. false withdraws and deletes the stored names. GET on the same route reads the setting.
  • MCP counter. The MCP server reports each tool call with POST /v1/mcp/ping {"tool": "upload_scene"} (any account token or org key). Only a short tool label is kept.

<verse-viewer>#

<script src="https://verse.ctruh.com/embed.js" async></script>

<verse-viewer
  src="palm-villa-0a1b2c3d4e5f"
  poster="https://verse.ctruh.com/ingest/palm-villa-0a1b2c3d4e5f.poster.png"
  autoplay-tour>
</verse-viewer>

That is the whole integration. The 3D engine runs in an iframe from the Verse origin, so your page needs no special headers; the element is lazy (no frame, no engine bytes until it comes within 300 px of the viewport), responsive (100 % of its container's width at 16:9), and keeps the embed scroll guard — on a phone a vertical swipe over the scene scrolls your page until the visitor taps into the scene; the mouse wheel does the same on desktop.

Attributes#

AttributeValue
srcscene id · .vpk / .glb / .fidelity.glb URL · a share linkrequired; a share link's share, look, bg and variant come along
share32-hex share tokenopens a private scene (private links)
posterimage URLshown until the scene draws (and if 3D cannot start)
backgroundrrggbb · transparent · grad:a,b · studio:neutral|warm|dark · image:… · hdr:…changes live
looklook preset, e.g. studio:warm, showroom
loadlazy (default) · eager · taptap shows a "View in 3D" button and loads nothing until it is pressed
autoplay-tourbooleanplays the owner's guided tour once the scene is in
aspect16:9 (default) · 4:3 · 1:1 · 3:4 · 9:16 · 21:9 · fillfill = the element's own CSS height
tiera · cpin the renderer: WebGPU where available (default) or WebGL2
hotspots · guard · fullscreen · analyticsfalse to turn offpins + tour · scroll guard · fullscreen button · view analytics
variant · qualitymaterial variant name · 4k

Changing an attribute re-mounts the viewer (except background, which changes in place).

Events#

DOM CustomEvents on the element; the payload is event.detail.

Eventdetail
load{ name, clusters?, streamed?, animations? } — the scene is in (streamed scenes keep refining)
ready{ tier, ttfi } — the engine booted (tier "A/B" WebGPU or "C" WebGL2)
progress{ drawn, total, fraction } — ~1 Hz streaming progress
error{ message, code? } — code: "degraded" when 3D cannot start here (the poster stays), "no-source" without src
hotspot{ id, label?, title? } — a hotspot was visited (click, tour, or viewer.goTo)
view-change{ position: [x,y,z], forward: [x,y,z] } — the camera moved (≤ 4 Hz, world metres)
tour{ playing, steps?, seconds? }

Every other viewer event (stage, variant, measure, …) is dispatched under its own name too.

Methods#

const el = document.querySelector("verse-viewer");
el.addEventListener("load", () => console.log("in"));
el.addEventListener("view-change", (e) => console.log(e.detail.position));

await el.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] }); // orbit camera: eye + pivot
await el.playTour();                                             // the owner's guided tour
el.stopTour();
const png = await el.screenshot();                               // Blob (image/png) of the current frame
el.activate();                                                   // mount now (skip lazy / tap)
el.viewer;                                                       // the full embed API: setVariant, setLights, exportVideo, …

Methods called before the scene has loaded wait for it. TypeScript: HTMLElementTagNameMap["verse-viewer"] is typed by verse-embed.d.ts (also shipped in @ctruhtech/verse-sdk).

React and Vue#

@ctruhtech/verse-react and @ctruhtech/verse-vue (in sdk/react, sdk/vue) are ~80-line wrappers with no dependencies beyond the framework: they load embed.js from your Verse origin once and render <verse-viewer>. Props mirror the attributes (camelCase; the element's load attribute is the loading prop), events arrive as callbacks / emits with the detail, and the ref exposes setCamera, playTour, stopTour, screenshot and viewer.

React#

import { useRef } from "react";
import { VerseViewer } from "@ctruhtech/verse-react";

export function Listing({ sceneId }) {
  const viewer = useRef(null);
  return (
    <>
      <VerseViewer
        ref={viewer}
        host="https://verse.ctruh.com"
        src={sceneId}
        autoplayTour
        onLoad={(d) => console.log("loaded", d.name)}
        onViewChange={(d) => console.log(d.position)}
      />
      <button onClick={() => viewer.current.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] })}>Front view</button>
    </>
  );
}

Vue 3#

<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";
import { VerseViewer } from "@ctruhtech/verse-vue";
const viewer = ref(null);
</script>

<template>
  <VerseViewer ref="viewer" host="https://verse.ctruh.com" :src="sceneId" autoplay-tour
    @load="(d) => console.log('loaded', d.name)" @view-change="(d) => console.log(d.position)" />
  <button @click="viewer.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] })">Front view</button>
</template>

No isCustomElement compiler option is needed: the wrapper renders the element itself.

Without a bundler: the Verse origin serves both wrappers at /sdk/react/index.js and /sdk/vue/index.js (CORS-enabled); map the framework with an import map. Complete pages are in the repository at sdk/examples/react.html and sdk/examples/vue.html.

The REST SDK#

@ctruhtech/verse-sdk — typed, dependency-free, ESM + CJS, Node 18+ and browsers. Without npm: import { VerseClient } from "https://verse.ctruh.com/sdk/verse-sdk.js".

Upload → ready → share#

import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { VerseClient } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";

const verse = new VerseClient({ baseUrl: "https://verse.ctruh.com", token: process.env.VERSE_TOKEN });

const bytes = await readFile("villa.glb");
const done = await verse.publish(bytes, {
  name: "palm-villa",
  resumable: true,                                   // chunked; survives a dropped connection
  onUploadProgress: (p) => console.log(`${Math.round(p.fraction * 100)} % uploaded`),
  onStage: (stage) => console.log("compiling:", stage), // preparing → queued → … → done
});
console.log(done.job, verse.shareLink(done));       // the scene id + its public link

publish() = upload() + waitForJob(); call them separately to store the job id and poll later (verse.job(id)). Failures throw VerseError with a friendly message and a stable code.

Publish settings#

await verse.scenes.setVisibility(sceneId, "private");     // "public" | "unlisted" | "private"
await verse.scenes.setBackground(sceneId, "studio:warm");
await verse.scenes.setDefaultExperience(sceneId, expId); // the tour the link plays

Private links#

A private scene answers 404 to everyone but its owner and holders of a share token. One call mints a token and builds the link; revoking it kills that link (and every embed using it) and nothing else:

const link = await verse.scenes.shares.link(sceneId);      // { id, shareToken, url, … } — token shown once
sendToClient(link.url);
// later
await verse.scenes.shares.revoke(sceneId, link.id);

Embed code#

const { element, iframe, url } = verse.embedCode(sceneId, { share: link.shareToken, autoplayTour: true });
// element: <script src=".../embed.js" async></script>\n<verse-viewer src="…" share="…" autoplay-tour></verse-viewer>
// iframe:  a responsive lazy iframe (for CMSs that strip scripts)
const oe = await verse.oembed(verse.shareLink(sceneId)); // what WordPress / Notion / Slack fetch

Analytics#

const a = await verse.analytics.scene(sceneId, { days: 30 });
console.log(a.views, a.uniqueViewers, a.time.medianSeconds, a.funnel);
const all = await verse.analytics.account({ days: 90 });   // + all.scenes[]
const csv = await verse.analytics.sceneCsv(sceneId);       // for a spreadsheet

Webhooks#

Register a URL; Verse POSTs to it when a scene you own finishes.

const hook = await verse.webhooks.create({
  url: "https://example.com/verse-hook",
  events: ["scene.ready", "scene.failed"],
});
saveSecret(hook.secret);           // shown ONCE
await verse.webhooks.test(hook.id); // a signed `ping`, right now
Eventdata
scene.ready{ job, scene, status: "done", url, vpkUrl?, stats? }
scene.failed{ job, scene, status: "error", error, code }
comment.added · version.promoted · config.changedsee api.md § Webhooks
ping{ hook, events } — only from webhooks.test()

Each delivery is POST {id, event, t, account, data} with headers X-Verse-Event, X-Verse-Delivery, X-Verse-Timestamp and X-Verse-Signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>")>. Answer any 2xx within 10 s. Anything else is retried — 3 tries, backoff 2 s then 8 s — and every attempt is in the delivery log (verse.webhooks.deliveries(hook.id), last 50). Hooks and logs persist with the rest of the server state (.verse-webhooks.json on the volume); ten hooks per account.

Receiver (Node, Express)#

Verify against the raw bytes, before parsing:

import express from "express";
import { verifyWebhook } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";

const app = express();
app.post("/verse-hook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), async (req, res) => {
  const ok = await verifyWebhook({
    secret: process.env.VERSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
    body: req.body,                                   // Buffer
    signature: req.get("X-Verse-Signature"),
    timestamp: req.get("X-Verse-Timestamp"),          // older than 5 min → false
  });
  if (!ok) return res.sendStatus(401);
  const { event, data } = JSON.parse(req.body.toString("utf8"));
  if (event === "scene.ready") await markListingLive(data.scene, data.url);
  res.sendStatus(204);
});

Deliveries can repeat (a retry after a slow 2xx): dedupe on X-Verse-Delivery.

Receiver (any language)#

import hmac, hashlib, time
def verify(secret: str, raw: bytes, sig: str, ts: str) -> bool:
    if abs(time.time() - int(ts)) > 300: return False
    want = "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), ts.encode() + b"." + raw, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(want, sig or "")

Proof#

web/test/fix-verify-devkit.mjs runs all of the above against a real server: the element on tier A and tier C in a plain page on another origin (lazy, responsive, scroll guard, private token, setCamera → view-change, screenshot, autoplay tour, hotspot, tap-to-load), the React and Vue example pages, the SDK from upload to revoked link, and a webhook receiver that fails once (retry, signature, delivery log).

Source: docs/developers.md · rendered in the browser from the repository's Markdown.

headings.text: Plan allowances: 402 and the Verse-Upgrade header#

/api.html:
Reference

API reference#

Everything Verse does is plain HTTP on one origin: upload a 3D file, poll the compile, get a signed streaming link, own it, share it privately, pin review comments on it, publish tours and posters, watch the platform. The playground, /studio, the embed SDK and the Blender, Unity and Unreal exporters are all clients of these routes — nothing below is internal.

  • Base URL: https://verse.ctruh.com for the hosted service, or your own origin (Run your own server). Examples write https://HOST.
  • New here? The API quickstart is the three-call version of this page. The Postman collection at /verse-api.postman_collection.json has every route below ready to run (generated from the same route table as the JS/TS SDK — scripts/gen-postman.mjs).
  • History: API changelog.

Every request and response shape on this page was executed against a live server before it was written down.

Conventions#

Requests and responses#

JSON in, JSON out, except where a body is raw bytes (GLB, PNG, upload parts) and where noted (204, 302, SSE). All /v1/* responses are Cache-Control: no-store (exception: /v1/pubkey, public, max-age=300). Scene artifacts under /ingest/* are immutable and cacheable (Cache-Control: public, immutable on hashed artifacts, ranges supported).

Error contract#

Every error the application generates carries the header X-Verse-Error: 1 and a JSON body {"error": "<human-readable cause>"}. Every status ≥ 400 from every route — 400, 401, 402, 404, 405, 409, 413, 429, 500, 503, 507 — follows the rule, static-file 404s included:

curl -sS -D - https://HOST/v1/ingest/does-not-exist
# HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
# X-Verse-Error: 1
# {"error":"unknown job"}

The header is the deterministic tell between the app and the network edge. Hosting proxies occasionally answer a request themselves — a bare 400 on a large or aborted body, a 502/504 on a timeout — and those responses do not carry it. Clients should treat:

  • error + X-Verse-Error: 1 → the app spoke. The error string is authoritative and actionable; do not blind-retry a 4xx (401/413/ 429/507 say exactly what to fix or wait for).
  • error without the header → an intermediary spoke; the app never saw or never finished the request. Transient — one retry is appropriate.

Success responses never carry the header. The bundled exporters implement exactly this rule (integrations/blender/verse_publish/net.py).

On the ingest routes the body also carries errorInfo — the structured twin of error (see Friendly errors). error is always a string.

Authentication#

Three credentials, each optional, each for a different job:

CredentialHeaderGrants
API key vk_…X-API-Key: vk_…upload quota in keyed mode (the operator provisioned ingest/.verse-keys.json; absent file = open mode, no key needed). Daily quota per key, default 512 MB; over → 429; unknown key → 401.
Account token (64 hex)Authorization: Bearer <token> — or the httpOnly verse_session cookie that POST /v1/account/login setsownership of what you publish, the account routes, /studio, moderation, ops reads, and the per-token ingest rate bucket. Returned once at POST /v1/account.
Share token (32 hex)?share=<token> on the URL, or X-Verse-Share: <token>read access to one private scene's artifacts and review comments. Minted by the owner, revocable individually.

A request carrying both an API key and account auth is quota-checked by the key and owned by the account.

People signing in through the website use a six-digit code sent by email or WhatsApp (Sign in); that creates the same verse_session cookie. The code routes (/v1/auth/*) exist for the website only and are not a stable API: scripts and plug-ins keep using the account token.

Rate limits#

Per client IP (first hop of X-Forwarded-For; loopback exempt) unless stated. Exceeding a bucket returns 429 with a body that says which.

BucketDefaultRoutes
Anonymous ingest6 / hour / IP (VERSE_INGEST_PER_HOUR)POST /v1/ingest, POST /v1/ingest/begin, POST /v1/ingest/url without a valid account token
Authenticated ingest20 / hour / token (VERSE_INGEST_PER_HOUR_TOKEN), independent of IPthe same routes with Authorization: Bearer
Publish30 / hour/v1/experience, /v1/tour, /v1/poster
Review posts60 / hourPOST /v1/review/<scene>
Account creation3 / dayPOST /v1/account
Login30 / hourPOST /v1/account/login
Dashboard reads and scene management240 / hour/v1/account/*, /v1/scenes/*, /v1/ops/*, review moderation
Telemetry240 / hourPOST /v1/telemetry
Analytics rows3600 / hour (VERSE_ANALYTICS_PER_HOUR) — about ten viewers behind one office networkPOST /v1/telemetry with kind view, look, act or batch
Healthrate-limited, no authGET /v1/health/deep
Assistant40 / hour (VERSE_ASSIST_PER_HOUR)POST /v1/assist

Plan allowances: 402 and the Verse-Upgrade header#

Every plan has monthly allowances (storage, bandwidth, API calls, Verse Homes, films, room captures, renders, seats, max upload — see Plans and pricing). The server enforces all of them. API calls are requests authenticated with an Authorization: Bearer header (an org API key or an account token); they are counted per account and per key for the billing month. /v1/plans, sign-in and webhooks are never counted, and a browser session (cookie) is not an API call.

At an allowance the route answers 402 Payment Required:

{
  "error": "Your API allowance of 5000 calls this month is used up. Starter includes 50000 API calls a month.",
  "code": "upgrade_required",
  "feature": "apiCallsPerMonth",
  "limit": 5000,
  "used": 5000,
  "plan": "free",
  "suggest": "starter",
  "upgrade_url": "https://verse.ctruh.com/pricing?from=api_call&suggest=starter",
  "nudge": { "type": "limit_100", "title": "…", "body": "…", "url": "https://verse.ctruh.com/n/…", "next": { "plan": "starter", "price": { "amount": 29, "currency": "USD" } } }
}

error, limit, used, plan and upgrade_url are always present (upgradeUrl, relative, is kept for older clients); feature names the allowance (storageGB, bandwidthGB, apiCallsPerMonth, plan2homePerMonth, filmsPerMonth, capturesPerMonth, rendersPerMonth, seats, rawUploadMB, …). The upgrade_url carries the trial offer while the account's trial runs (&offer=trial). A 402 is not retryable until the plan changes or the billing month resets.

Near an allowance (80 % or more of API calls used) every API response carries a Verse-Upgrade header:

Verse-Upgrade: https://verse.ctruh.com/pricing?suggest=starter&from=nudge_limit_80; meter=apiCallsPerMonth; used=82%; plan=free; next=starter

Viewers are never refused: a published scene keeps opening when its owner is over the month's bandwidth (it is served at a lighter quality).

Endpoint index#

AreaRoutes
IngestGET /v1/limits · POST /v1/ingest · GET /v1/ingest/<job> · POST /v1/ingest/<job>/contact · POST /v1/ingest/url · POST /v1/ingest/begin · `PUTGET /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId>·POST /v1/ingest/commit/<uploadId>`
AccountsPOST /v1/account · POST /v1/account/login · POST /v1/account/logout · GET /v1/account · GET /v1/account/scenes · GET /v1/account/stats · GET /v1/account/analytics[.csv] · `GETPOST /v1/account/webhooks·DELETE /v1/account/webhooks/<id>·GET /v1/account/webhooks/<id>/deliveries`
ScenesPOST /v1/scenes/<id>/claim · DELETE /v1/scenes/<id> · PATCH /v1/scenes/<id> · GET /v1/scenes/<id>/stats · `POSTGET /v1/scenes/<id>/share·DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/share/<shareId>·GET /v1/scenes/<id>/current·/v1/scenes/<id>/versions[/<n>[/diff/activate/file/stage]]·GET /v1/scenes/<id>/heatmap·GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics[.csv]·GET /v1/scenes/<id>/report[.csv]·GETPOST /v1/scenes/<id>/report/links·DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/report/links/<linkId>·GET /v1/reports/<token>[.csv]·GETPUTDELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/enquiry·GET /v1/scenes/<id>/experiences·PUTGET /v1/scenes/<id>/experience·PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/ground·GETPUT /v1/scenes/<id>/config`
EmbedsGET /oembed · GET /embed (the lazy embed card)
Review comments`POSTGET /v1/review/<scene>·DELETE /v1/review/<scene>/<id>·POST /v1/review/<scene>/<id>/resolve`
PublishingPOST /v1/experience · `GETPUT /v1/experience/<id>·POST /v1/experience/<id>/media·POST /v1/tour·POST /v1/poster`
PresenceGET /v1/room/<room>/events (SSE) · POST /v1/room/<room>/pose · POST /v1/room/<room>/signal · POST /v1/room/<room>/leave · POST /v1/tour/invite · GET /v1/tour/invite/<code> · GET /t/<code>
SigningGET /v1/pubkey
OperationsGET /v1/health/deep · GET /v1/status · GET /v1/ops/ingest-stats · GET /v1/ops/errors · GET /v1/ops/leads · GET /v1/config · POST /v1/telemetry
Floor plan to 3D homePOST /v1/plan2home/analyze · POST /v1/plan2home/build · GET /v1/plan2home/status
AssistantPOST /v1/assist (SSE) · GET /v1/assist/status
Compile fleetGET /v1/work/claim · GET /v1/work/<id>/source · GET /v1/work/<id>/images · POST /v1/work/<id>/stage · POST /v1/work/<id>/result

Ingest#

GET /v1/limits#

What an uploader should know before choosing a file. Public, no auth, Cache-Control: public, max-age=60. The app's upload screen and its preflight are driven by this body; guide: What you can upload.

curl -sS https://HOST/v1/limits
{
  "limits": { "maxUploadBytes": 536870912, "maxUploadMB": 512, "maxPreparedUploadMB": 2048, "compileWallClockMin": 45, "compileAttemptMin": 30,
              "maxAttempts": 3, "concurrentCompiles": 2, "queueMax": 32, "maxSplats": 4000000,
              "uploadsPerHour": { "anonymous": 6, "account": 20 }, "jobRecordTtlMin": 120, … },
  "formats": [ { "ext": "glb", "name": "GLB (binary glTF 2.0)", "kind": "mesh", "note": "…" }, … ],
  "extensions": { "decoded": ["KHR_draco_mesh_compression", "KHR_mesh_quantization", "EXT_texture_webp", "KHR_texture_basisu", "EXT_meshopt_compression", "KHR_meshopt_compression"],
                  "unsupported": ["EXT_texture_avif", "KHR_gaussian_splatting"] },
  "textures": { "streamedMaterials": 2048, "streamBudgetMB": 768, "streamSizePx": 2048, "heroTextures": 12, "heroSizePx": 4096 },
  "recommended": { "triangles": 3000000, "textures": 400, "textureSizePx": 2048, "fileMB": 170, "basis": "…", "note": "…" },
  "timing": { "secondsPerMB": 8, "floorS": 15, "source": "formula", "samples": 0 },
  "queue": { "active": 1, "compiling": 1, "waiting": 0 },
  "storage": { "freeMB": 3811, "ok": true },
  "notify": { "email": true },
  "scanImport": { "extensions": ["usdz", "usd", "usda", "usdc", "glb", "gltf", "ply", "obj", "zip", "e57", "las", "laz", "xyz", "pts", "splat"],
                  "maxUploadMB": 512, "convertBudgetMin": 15, "cleanupBudgetMin": 10, "packAttemptMin": 30, "compileWallClockMin": 45,
                  "maxCloudPoints": 200000000, "maxSplats": 4000000,
                  "up": ["auto", "x", "y", "z", "-x", "-y", "-z"], "units": ["auto", "m", "cm", "mm", "in", "ft"], "linkImport": false }
}
FieldMeaning
limitsenforced — the server's own constants and environment
recommendedrecommendations, not limits — the largest scene tested every release; larger scenes are attempted
texturesthe texture streaming budget (the compiler's defaults unless the server's environment overrides them)
timingtypical build seconds per source MB — source: "history" once the server has enough completed builds of its own, else the "formula" (~8 s/MB)
queuelive: jobs in flight, compiles running, jobs waiting for a slot
notify.emailwhether this server can email uploaders (see contact)
scanImportImport a scan: the capture extensions, the same upload cap, the budget of each step a capture goes through (converter, cleanup, packing attempt, whole job), the point and splat caps, the accepted X-Verse-Up / X-Verse-Units values, and linkImport: false (a hosted-tour link is recognised, not fetched)

POST /v1/ingest#

Upload a 3D file; the compile runs in the background.

  • Body: the raw bytes — no multipart. A GLB (Content-Type: model/gltf-binary), a Gaussian-splat capture (.splat antimatter15 or INRIA 3DGS binary .ply), a point cloud (.ply with x y z vertices, .las/.laz LAS 1.2–1.4 point formats 0–10, .e57), an IFC building model (.ifc, IFC2x3 / IFC4), a USD scene (.usdz, .usd, .usda, .usdc — one self-contained file; see IFC and USD), or an FBX / OBJ model, alone or in a .zip with its textures (see FBX and OBJ). Max 512 MB one-shot; larger files (up to the plan's raw cap, 2 GB on Free) go through the resumable upload and are prepared on arrival.
  • Headers (optional): X-Verse-Name — slug prefix for the scene id ([a-z0-9-_]); X-Verse-Kind: splat | cloud | ifc | usd | fbx | obj | ply (a PLY mesh) — force the kind (otherwise sniffed: ply\n magic → splat when the 3DGS fields are present, else cloud; LASF / ASTM-E57 magic → cloud; ISO-10303-21 → ifc; #usda, PXR-USDC or a .usdz zip → usd; Kaydara FBX Binary or an ASCII ; FBX header → fbx; OBJ text → obj; a zip holding an .fbx / .obj → fbx / obj — for IFC/USD/FBX/OBJ the bytes decide and the header is only a hint; a 32-byte-aligned body with neither the VPK1 nor glTF magic → splat); X-Verse-Units: m | cm | mm | in | ft — the file's unit for an OBJ (see FBX and OBJ) and, 4.0, for a scan capture that does not declare one (OBJ, PLY, text clouds, E57, LAS; otherwise read from the capture's height); X-Verse-Up: auto | x | y | z | -x | -y | -z — which file axis is up for a capture (otherwise from the surfaces, then the format's convention; GLB and USD keep the frame they declare); X-Verse-Scan: clean | off — force or skip the scan cleanup (levelled floor, debris removed, small holes filled, baked-in light evened out) instead of letting detection decide; the record's scan says what was done — guide: Import a scan; X-Verse-Source — tool attribution; X-API-Key in keyed mode; Authorization: Bearer to own the scene; X-Verse-Bake: preview | final — bake the lighting of a live-lit GLB on the server before compiling (2.7); X-Verse-As: product | interior | building | exterior — say what the file is (the upload card's "3D model or scene?" answer: a model is a product, a scene is walkable); without it the classifier decides; X-Verse-Path: fidelity | streamed — (2.8) take the Fidelity road: the Draco-decoded file itself is published as ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb (textures at source resolution, no compile, seconds), opened by /view?glb=; without the header an upload streams as before and the record's classification says what the shared classifier would pick; X-Verse-Look: studio:neutral|warm|dark[,bg:rrggbb] — the studio preset and backdrop the share link opens with (?look=).
  • Draco-compressed, KHR-quantized and WebP/KTX2-textured GLBs are accepted and normalized server-side.
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest \
  -H "Content-Type: model/gltf-binary" -H "X-Verse-Name: docs-demo" \
  --data-binary @scene.glb
# HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
# {"job":"docs-demo-718035483f84"}
  • Validation: right after the upload, before a compile is queued, the server inspects the file (magic bytes; for a GLB its JSON chunk — meshes, triangles, external references, required extensions). A file it cannot build still answers 202 {job}; the job's first poll is then status: "error" with a friendly error. Nothing was compiled and any key quota is refunded.
  • Response 202: { "job": "<id>" }. The job id is the scene id. - Errors: 400 malformed · 401 unknown/missing key (keyed mode) · 413 over 512 MB · 429 rate limit or quota (body says which) · 503 compile queue full · 507 storage full — refused before the body is read when free space is below max(VERSE_MIN_FREE_MB, 3× the declared size).

GET /v1/ingest/<job>#

Fidelity mode (2.8) adds to a done record: path ("fidelity" | "streamed"), glbUrl (https://HOST/ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb), classification ({ kind, path, plan, evidence, requested, resolved, reason? } — the verdict with its evidence: meshes, triangles, textures, maxTextureDim, decodedMB, longestSide, lights, lighting), look, digest (sha256:<hex> of the artifact) and signature (base64 Ed25519 over that digest under the server's signing key, the .vpk trailer's twin), stats.mode: "fidelity"; arUrl as for a streamed scene.

Poll every few seconds until status leaves "compiling". Small models compile in seconds; multi-million-triangle scans in minutes. estimateS is the expected build time, calibrated against this server's recent builds of similar size (falling back to ~8 s per source MB, floor 15 s).

A finished record may carry prepare: { inputBytes, outputBytes, resized, meshesInstanced, seconds } when the server ran verse-prepare on the upload (it does not when the file arrived with the marker), and its fixes line says what changed.

While compiling:

Never counts up: it includes the queue wait while queued, and once a build overruns its estimate etaS is 0, overEstimate is true and the label reads "Finishing up — taking a little longer than usual". contacttrue once a contact is attached (never the contact itself)

When done:

FieldMeaning
