Reply: code (7 chars, no 0/o/1/l/i), the absolute url (/t/<code> on the request's origin — X-Forwarded-Proto/Host are honoured), room, scene, expiresAt (ms; VERSE_TOUR_INVITE_TTL_H, default 24 h) and the landing path. Cache-Control: no-store.
Errors: 400 not an ingest scene / bad room / torn body; 429 over VERSE_TOUR_INVITES_PER_HOUR (default 60) per address per hour (loopback exempt in development).
The table holds 5 000 invites; past that the oldest tenth is dropped.
GET /V1/TOUR/INVITE/<CODE>#

{code, room, scene, expiresAt, landing} for a live invite, 404 for an unknown or expired code. no-store.

GET /T/<CODE>#

The link people open. 302 to /view?vpk=<scene>&room=<room>&live=1 (no-store); an unknown or expired code answers a small 404 HTML page ("This tour link has expired"). live=1 makes the viewer join as a guest: the Enter gate on phones, then the optional name chip, then following the host. ?room=<room>&host=1 hosts a room at once; a plain ?room= is the 2.7 viewer with the tour bar.

POST /V1/ROOM/<ROOM>/LEAVE#
Copy
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/room/docs-room/leave -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"id":"docs-viewer-1"}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

A page that closes says so (the viewer sends it with sendBeacon on pagehide), and the peer is dropped from the roster and rebroadcast at once instead of lingering for the 10 s TTL — the guests' "the agent left" chip must not wait on a sweep. Body ≤ 256 B, {id} (4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-]); 400 bad id. Optional: a client that never sends it (the embed's own room join, older viewers) is swept after 10 s as before.

LIVE-TOUR SIGNALS AND FLAGS#
flags.host on the pose record marks the tour's host (the host also carries presenter: guests follow the presenter mechanics).
kind: "ping", to: "*", data: {pos: [x, y, z], name} — "look here": every screen draws a pulsing ring at that world point for a few seconds.
kind: "end", to: "*", data: {by} — the host ended the tour; guests release their cameras.
kind: "handover" (addressed) makes the recipient the host as well as the presenter.
Guests count in analytics as one act: "livetour" row per session (liveTours / live_tour_sessions in the scene report).
Signing#
GET /v1/pubkey#

The deployment's Ed25519 public key. No auth; Cache-Control: public, max-age=300.

Copy
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/pubkey
# {"alg":"Ed25519","spki":"MCowBQYDK2VwAyEABHN2qIj3nOB4cvTPeA0erREzZQC1G4kpkunME6GA0B8="}

spki is base64 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, importable as-is with crypto.subtle.importKey("spki", der, { name: "Ed25519" }, false, ["verify"]). The viewer fetches it from the host page's origin — the page embedding a scene is the trust anchor — and reports signed: true | false | "unverified". It must be identical across deploys; a changed spki means the key was not persisted and earlier scenes now read signed: false (they still load).

Operations#

Two more operations routes are not a developer surface: GET /v1/status feeds the public status page, and GET /v1/ops/errors is the operator-only error ring.

GET /v1/health/deep#

No auth, rate-limited, cheap by contract (in-memory counters plus a touch/unlink probe on the volume — never a compile). 200 when every check passes, 503 otherwise.

Copy
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/health/deep
Copy
{
  "ok": true,
  "version": "4.0.0",
  "checks": {
    "volumeWritable": true,
    "compilerPresent": true,
    "signingKey": true,
    "disk": { "freeMB": 491739, "totalMB": 948534, "usedPct": 48 },
    "lastIngest": { "t": 1790833829990, "ok": true },
    "ingestLastHour": { "attempts": 18, "done": 16, "failed": 2 },
    "telemetryWritable": true
  }
}

disk.ok turns false below 512 MB free; lastIngest is null before the first upload and carries error on a failure. A server storing scenes in a bucket (VERSE_STORAGE=s3) adds storage: { backend: "s3", bucket, reachable }, and an unreachable bucket fails the check.

GET /v1/ops/ingest-stats#

Account auth required (any valid account); 401 otherwise. The last 24 h from the persisted ring of the last 200 ingest outcomes (ingest/.ingest-log.jsonl), plus the client-side failure beacons:

Copy
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/ops/ingest-stats -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
Copy
{
  "last24h": { "attempts": 68, "done": 61, "failed": 7, "byReason": { "failed": 7, "evicted": 46 }, "p50s": 5, "p95s": 19 },
  "recent": [ { "t": 1790831611415, "idHash": "ace65061d8ab", "sizeMB": 77.32, "outcome": "done", "seconds": 613 } ],
  "telemetry24h": { "canaryFails": 0, "uploadFails": 1, "loadErrors": 0, "lastCanaryFail": null,
                    "lastUploadFail": { "t": 1790832030821, "detail": "HTTP 400: …", "phase": "upload" } }
}

Rows also carry attempts, healed, repaired (verification repairs), fallback and the taxonomy code when they apply. Outcomes: done · safe-mode-used (landed only on a lighter rung of the self-healing ladder — the early warning before hard OOMs) · classic-fallback (delivered through the lossless fallback) · timeout · oom · failed (application error: bad input, ENOSPC…) · storage-full (507 at preflight) · evicted (disk-budget reclaim; not an attempt). Scene ids are hashed. Guide: Monitor production.

GET /v1/ops/leads#

The contacts uploaders attached (name, phone, email, job, whether the email went out), newest first, max 500. This is personal data, so it is gated harder than ingest-stats: Authorization: Bearer <VERSE_ADMIN_TOKEN>, or an account whose id is listed in VERSE_OPS_ACCOUNTS (comma-separated). 401 without auth, 403 for any other account.

Copy
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/ops/leads -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERSE_ADMIN_TOKEN"
# {"count":1,"emailConfigured":true,"slackConfigured":true,
#  "leads":[{"job":"villa-3b0cc31202bd","name":"Asha Rao","email":"asha@example.com","phone":"+919876543210",
#            "consent":true,"at":1790873084372,"emailed":true,"emailKind":"live","status":"done","url":"https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/villa-3b0cc31202bd.vpk"}]}
GET /v1/status#

Public, rate-limited with the health bucket: the JSON behind the status page — health, the self-canary's last 24 h and a client-error count. No customer data.

GET /v1/ops/errors#

Account auth (any valid account), as /v1/ops/ingest-stats: the operator dashboard's grouped errors { groups, status } — client beacons, failed ingests, server crashes. Samples can name scenes, hence the auth.

GET /v1/config#

Public client knobs, read once per page by the viewer: { "cdnBase": "", "interior": "ingest/<id>.vpk" | null, "version": "4.0.0" } — cdnBase is the CDN origin the client should range public scenes against, or empty for "everything on this origin"; interior is the deployment's public show flat when it has one (the guided tour uses it to teach Walk and the floor plan); version is the release this server runs (also in /v1/health/deep).

Floor plan to 3D home#

Turn a brochure floor plan into a furnished, walkable scene. Guide: Floor plan to 3D home. Both POSTs go through the same gates as POST /v1/ingest: the per-account/per-IP rate bucket, the key pre-check before the body, and the key and daily quota after it. A build counts as an upload of the generated GLB.

Privacy: the image goes to the Anthropic API only when the server has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set. Without it, only the built-in plan reader runs, and nothing leaves the server.

GET /v1/plan2home/status#

200 { "enabled": true, "ai": false, "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "styles": [{ "id": "modern-indian", "label": "Modern Indian", "blurb": "…" }, …], "defaultStyle": "modern-indian", "maxImageBytes": 25165824 }. ai is true when the AI reader is on.

POST /v1/plan2home/analyze#
Body: the raw image (PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF), at most 24 MB. For a PDF, the first JPEG page image is read.
X-Verse-Hints (optional): JSON, plain or URI-encoded. All fields are optional:
areaSqft or areaSqm, with areaKind set to carpet (the default), builtup or super;
widthM, the outside width in metres (beats the area);
bhk, style, city and name.
200: { plan, stats, svg, ai: { used, model?, error?, tries? }, repair, validation, frame, timings }.
plan is the plan document. It is in metres, with x to the right and y down, and holds walls, openings and rooms (id, name, type, rects, area, center). Each opening has kind, at, width, dir, rooms, entrance and added:
kind is door, window or open. An open gap is an archway or a kitchen open to the living room: no leaf, and you walk through it.
added: true marks a door the reader put in because the drawing didn't show one.
repair is { added, entrance, unreachable }:
added is how many doors were added;
entrance is "moved" or "added" when the entrance was put right, else null;
unreachable lists the rooms that no legal door can reach (never through a bathroom, never in an outside wall). Normally it is empty.
validation is { ok, problems: [{ code, message, rooms? }] }: what still looks off after the readers and the repair. code is unreachable, overlapping_openings, overlapping_rooms, tiny_room (under 1.5 m² and not a toilet, store, utility or pooja), area_mismatch (the rooms' total more than 15 % off the printed total or the areaSqft / areaSqm hint; 25 % against a built-up or super area) or room_area_mismatch (a room more than 25 % off its printed area or dimensions). Check rooms lists them; the build does not refuse them (only unreachable rooms do).
ai.tries (only when the plan was read more than once) lists each reading: { model, problems? | error? }. A reading that fails validation is read again by a stronger model (see VERSE_PLAN_ESCALATE), and the reading with the fewest problems wins.
frame is { imageW, imageH, pxPerM, origin, deskew? }: image pixel = (plan metres + origin) × pxPerM, before the deskew rotation (radians, about the image centre) is undone. Use it to draw the plan over the upload.
stats gives the rooms by type, the carpet area and the BHK.
svg is the plan drawn for display.
ai.error is set when the AI reader was on but failed. In that case the built-in reader's plan is returned.
Errors:
413: over the size limit.
415: not a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF.
422: no plan could be read, or the image is not a floor plan (a photo of a room, a render). The error field says why, in words meant for the user.
503: two plans are already being read; retry after Retry-After.
POST /v1/plan2home/build#
Body (JSON, ≤ 1 MB): { "plan": <plan from analyze, edited>, "style": "modern-indian" | "scandinavian" | "luxury" | "minimal", "name": "Sunrise 2BHK" }.
What it does: generates the furnished GLB. Before publishing, it walks the home from the entrance on a 10 cm grid.
202: { job, id, statusUrl, experienceUrl, checks, stats }.
Follow statusUrl (GET /v1/ingest/<job>) exactly as for an upload.
When the job is done, <id>.stage.json holds the spawn at the living-room entrance, with a walk view. ingest/exp-<hex>.verse.json holds one hotspot per room and a guided tour, and it is the scene's default experience when an account owns the scene.
experienceUrl opens the scene with the room hotspots.
Errors:
400: the plan is malformed.
422 { "code": "unreachable_rooms", "unreachable": [{ "id", "name" }] }: a room cannot be reached from the entrance (usually a missing door). Nothing is published. The plan is built exactly as sent, so the build adds no doors. Add one in the plan (Check rooms: Edit doors), or send the plan that analyze returned, which is already repaired.
503 server_busy: the compile queue is full.
Assistant#

The endpoint behind Ask Verse, the site assistant. Guide: Ask Verse. It has no server-side side effects and no access to accounts, tokens, scenes or files: it returns text plus UI actions from a fixed whitelist, which the page validates again and runs itself.

POST /v1/assist#
Body (JSON, ≤ 48 KB): { "messages": [{ "role": "user" | "assistant", "content": "…" }], "context": { "surface": "landing" | "app" | "studio" | "docs", "path": "/app", "sceneLoaded": true } }. The first and last message must be from the user. At most 20 messages, 1,000 characters in the newest one.
Response: 200 text/event-stream. Each data: line is one JSON event:
Copy
data: {"type":"text","delta":"Opening the upload panel."}
data: {"type":"action","action":{"type":"open_upload"}}
data: {"type":"done","mode":"ai"}

text events are appended in order; action events arrive after the text; done carries the mode that answered (ai or basic); an error event means the reply was cut short and no action should run.

Actions (the whole list): navigate {path} (only /, /app, /studio, /docs/ and product-page sections), open_upload, load_demo {name}, start_tour {surface, chapter?}, set_view {mode} (walk, orbit, tour, stop_tour, minimap, measure), export_video, open_review, share_link, open_docs {page, section?} (public docs pages only), show_limits {limits}. At most 3 per reply.
Errors carry { "error": "…", "message": "…" }, where message is written for the visitor: 400 (malformed or too long), 403 (cross-site request), 429 (per-IP bucket), 503 (daily cap reached, busy, or unavailable).
Copy
curl -N -X POST "$VERSE/v1/assist" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"how big can my file be?"}],"context":{"surface":"landing"}}'
GET /v1/assist/status#

{ "mode": "ai" } when the server has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, { "mode": "basic" } otherwise (a deterministic local responder: curated intents plus a search over the public docs headings).

POST /v1/telemetry#

Client telemetry sink. Body ≤ 1 MB, one batch per POST → one line of ingest/.telemetry.jsonl (rotated at ~32 MB, one rotation kept), forwarded as ndjson when VERSE_TELEMETRY_URL is set. Always 204.

Failure-beacon rows — the only record of failures the app never saw — carry a top-level kind:

kind	Sent by	When	Fields
upload-fail	the playground	an upload failed client-side: HTTP error, network error, or the job polled to error	detail (HTTP <status>: <message>), phase (upload = the POST itself failed, incl. edge failures; compile = server-side)
load-error	the playground	a share link failed to load in the viewer	detail, phase: "load"
canary-fail	the external hourly canary	its end-to-end upload probe failed	detail
look	the viewer (2.5.0)	every 2 s while a scene is live and visible (batched, one POST per ~10 s)	pos [x,y,z], yaw (degrees), streaming, stalled, walking, scene, session, vid, t — folded by GET /v1/scenes/<id>/heatmap and /analytics
view	the viewer	once per scene per page	dev (phone/tablet/desktop), os, app (in-app browser or none), via (direct/share/embed), ref (referring site's class: whatsapp, instagram, facebook, linkedin, twitter, youtube, google, search, email, other, none), scene, session, vid, t
act	the viewer	first input on the scene; enquiry clicks; hotspot opens and card links; Ask Verse questions	act: interact, enquiry, hotspot, link or question; target (the hotspot id) on hotspot / link
batch	the viewer	wraps up to 60 of the rows above	rows: [...]; stored as one line per row

view, look, act and batch rows have their own rate bucket and are rebuilt from a whitelist before they are stored (see Analytics).

Schema: Telemetry.

Compile fleet: /v1/work/*#

Pull API for external compile workers (tools/verse-worker). Every route requires Authorization: Bearer $VERSE_WORKER_TOKEN; while the variable is unset the routes answer 404, a wrong token 401. Jobs unclaimed for 10 s, or claimed but silent for 20 min, fall back to the origin's local compiler, so zero workers is exactly the single-box behaviour.

Route	What
GET /v1/work/claim	Claim the oldest unclaimed job. 204 = nothing to do; 200 = { "id", "images": bool, "source": "/v1/work/<id>/source" }. X-Verse-Worker: <name> is credited as workedBy.
GET /v1/work/<id>/source	The uploaded GLB bytes.
GET /v1/work/<id>/images	The KTX2 RGBA sidecar for --images, or 404.
POST /v1/work/<id>/stage	{ "stage": "<a-z->" } progress shown live to the uploader; 204. "worker-failed" hands the job back to the origin immediately.
POST /v1/work/<id>/result	The finished .vpk bytes; stats in X-Verse-Tris / X-Verse-Clusters. 204; 410 = the job already finished elsewhere.

The origin signs delivered files itself; workers never hold the key. Splat jobs are never offered to the fleet.

Fleet bake. A worker that sends X-Verse-Caps: bake on its claims is counted for "Bake for me" splits (seen in the last 15 s) and is offered bake parts before compile jobs; workers without the header never see them. A bake is split into 1 + (such workers), at most 8, parts (VERSE_BAKE_PARTS on the origin forces a count); part 0 runs on the origin. A bake-part claim answers:

Copy
{ "id": "villa-9f3a01b2c4d5~bake2", "kind": "bake-part", "quality": "final",
  "part": 2, "parts": 3, "deadlineS": 1041, "source": "/v1/work/villa-9f3a01b2c4d5~bake2/source" }

The worker downloads source (the prepared GLB the origin is baking), runs verse-compile --bake <quality> in.glb --part <part>/<parts> --deadline-s <deadlineS> -o part.vbp, heartbeats POST …/stage ({"stage":"baking"}), and posts the part file to POST …/result (204; 410/404 = the bake already finished without it). The origin drops it into its coordinator's part directory; a part with a different plan fingerprint is ignored, and a part that does not arrive in time is baked on the origin — a slow or vanished worker costs time, never the bake. deadlineS is what is left of the origin's own deadline.

JS SDK#

@ctruhtech/verse-sdk (since 2.6.0; 4.0.0 today) is the typed, dependency-free client for every route on this page — upload (one-shot and resumable, progress, cancel), job polling with stage callbacks, scenes, share tokens, versions and diffs, review comments, heatmap, publishing, presence, operations, and embedViewer() over the embed SDK. ESM + CJS + full typings; Node 18+ and browsers. Full reference with a runnable example per method: docs/sdk.md. Served without a package manager at /sdk/verse-sdk.js (same headers as embed.js):

Copy
import { VerseClient } from "https://HOST/sdk/verse-sdk.js"; // or the package, once it is on npm
const verse = new VerseClient({ baseUrl: "https://HOST", token: "<account token>" });
const done = await verse.publish(bytes, { name: "chair", onStage: (s) => console.log(s) });
console.log(verse.shareLink(done));

The route table behind this page, the Postman collection and the SDK is scripts/api-routes.mjs; scripts/api-parity.mjs fails when any of the three drifts from the server's dispatch.

4.0 developer kit: the <verse-viewer> element, React and Vue wrappers, analytics.*, embedCode(), scenes.shares.link(), webhooks.test() and verifyWebhook() — one page of copy-paste examples in developers.md.

The original single-file verse-sdk.js (v0: VerseClient({ endpoint, apiKey }), ingest(), mount()) stays served at /verse-sdk.js for existing pages; new code should use @ctruhtech/verse-sdk.

Embed SDK#

One script, embed.js, mounts the engine in an iframe from the Verse origin — full reference in embed-sdk.md, guide in Embed the viewer. What ships in embeds versus the playground:

Playground ↔ embed parity#
Feature	Playground	Embed SDK	Notes
Streamed .vpk / .vsp / GLB / splat loading	✔	✔	same engine, same routes (same-origin only)
Orbit / pinch / wheel camera	✔	✔	shared camera-controls.js
Walk mode + analog move	✔	✔ walk() / move()	no on-screen joystick in embeds; feed move() from your UI
Animations, picking, materials, sun, exposure, DoF, emitters, props, sounds, rooms, tours, experiences	✔	✔	see embed-sdk.md
Voice + presenter mode (2.7)	✔ viewers panel	✔ joinRoom(id, { voice }), present(), setVoice(), room / peer / speaking events	same voice.js / presenter.js inside the iframe; the follower veil renders in-frame
Video export	✔ chip + __verseExportVideo	✔ exportVideo() / cancelExport()	embeds hand the bytes to the host page instead of auto-downloading — guide
Review pins	✔ Review chip	✔ opt-in review: true, setReviewMode() / getComments()	same review.js inside the iframe; owner moderation stays playground/studio-only
Private scenes	✔ ?share=	✔ share option	the token covers bytes and review calls
HDR display output	✔ ?hdr=auto default	opt-in hdr: "auto" | 1 (default SDR)	embeds never shift a host page's colours uninvited
On-demand rendering	opt-in ?render=demand (default on battery)	✔ default	embeds park when nothing changes
Upload / ingest UI	✔	✘	use verse-sdk.js from your own page
Stats HUD / inspector / editor / minimap	✔	✘	playground chrome; embeds expose progress events instead
Video export in embeds#

viewer.exportVideo({ duration, fps, height, format, bitrate }) records the scene's tour inside the iframe and resolves { blob, mimeType, name, width, height, frames, cancelled }; export-progress events stream meanwhile; cancelExport() resolves { cancelled: true }. Message protocol for non-SDK hosts: verse:export-video down, verse:event {name:"export-progress"} up, verse:export-video-done with the transferred ArrayBuffer (or { id, error }), verse:export-video-cancel. Details and a copy-paste page: Export a flythrough video.

Exporters#

All three speak this API — POST /v1/ingest (resumable above 100 MB where implemented) → poll → hand the user url — and all three honour the error contract (verbatim app errors, one retry on edge failures only, 30-minute budget).

Blender — integrations/blender/verse_publish, the Verse Publish extension (Blender 4.2+, stdlib-only): N-panel "Verse" tab, export → upload → live link with progress, cancel, copy/open. Machine-tested end to end (web/test/fix-verify-blender.mjs). Guide: Publish from Blender.
Unity — integrations/unity/com.ctruh.verse-publish, a UPM package (Unity 2021.3+, glTFast): Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish Scene window. The protocol layer is UnityEngine-free C#, replayed live by web/test/fix-verify-unity.mjs; verified in Unity 6000.6 on URP (Boat Attack) and HDRP scenes (smoke test). Guide: Publish from Unity.
Unreal — integrations/unreal/VersePublish, an editor plugin (UE 5.3+): Tools ▸ Verse ▸ Publish to Verse. HTTP protocol verified by integrations/unreal/protocol-reference.mjs + web/test/fix-verify-unreal.mjs; compiled and clicked through in Unreal Engine 5.8.3 by the editor automation test that ships with it (smoke test). Guide: Publish from Unreal.

The original single-file tools/verselink-* references remain as minimal protocol examples.

/api-quickstart.html:
Reference

Verse API — Quickstart#

Everything Verse does is a plain HTTP API — the playground, the embed SDK, and the Blender, Unity and Unreal exporters are all clients of the same endpoints. Anything that can send an HTTP request (a game-engine plugin, a Blender add-on, a CI pipeline, curl) can turn a 3D file into a signed, streamed share link.

  • Base URL: https://verse.ctruh.com (self-hosted: your origin)
  • Postman collection: /verse-api.postman_collection.json — import and try every call
  • Full reference: docs/api.md · Embed SDK: docs/embed-sdk.md · JS/TS client: docs/sdk.md (@ctruhtech/verse-sdk — not on npm yet; build it from sdk/ or load /sdk/verse-sdk.js)

Authentication#

Two modes, set by the server operator:

  • Open mode (no key file configured — current default): no auth header needed. Uploads are rate-limited to 6/hour per IP (20/hour per account token sent as Authorization: Bearer); publish endpoints (tour/poster/ experience) to 30/hour per IP. Files up to 512 MB, or 2 GB when prepared and sent through the resumable upload; GET /v1/limits returns the live numbers.
  • Keyed mode: send X-Api-Key: <your key> on uploads. Each key has a daily upload quota (default 512 MB/day). Bad or missing key → 401; over quota → 429. Keys are provisioned by the operator in ingest/.verse-keys.json (see docs/api.md).

The core flow: file in → share link out#

1. Upload — POST the raw bytes (no multipart):

curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/ingest" \
  -H "Content-Type: model/gltf-binary" \
  -H "X-Verse-Name: my-apartment" \
  --data-binary @scene.glb
# → 202 {"job":"my-apartment-1a2b3c4d5e6f"}

Accepted inputs, auto-detected by magic bytes:

You sendDetected asCompiles to
.glb (binary glTF; Draco + KTX2 supported)mesh scenestreamed .vpk
.ply or .splat (Gaussian-splat capture)splatstreamed .vsp
.ply (points), .las / .laz, .e57, .xyz / .ptspoint cloudstreamed point cloud
.ifc, .usdz / .usd*, .fbx, .obj (alone or zipped with textures), PLY meshconverted to GLB on the serverstreamed .vpk
a phone / LiDAR capture, a 3D tour export bundle's .zipscan (cleaned up first)Fidelity or streamed — see Import a scan

Force the kind for headerless formats with X-Verse-Kind (splat, cloud, ifc, usd, fbx, obj, ply); the full header list (bake, Fidelity path, look, scan, up axis, units) is in POST /v1/ingest. X-Verse-Name is optional (lowercase letters, digits, -, _); it prefixes the id. Max body: 512 MB (20 GB for a prepared GLB through the resumable upload).

2. Poll the job until done (typical: ~8 s per source MB, floor 15 s — the record carries a live stage and estimateS so you can show honest progress):

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/ingest/my-apartment-1a2b3c4d5e6f"
{
  "status": "done",
  "url":    "https://…/?vpk=ingest/my-apartment-1a2b3c4d5e6f.vpk",
  "vpkUrl": "https://…/ingest/my-apartment-1a2b3c4d5e6f.vpk",
  "stats":  { "tris": 182340, "clusters": 3271 },
  "signed": true
}

While compiling you get {"status":"compiling","stage":"…","estimateS":…}; on failure {"status":"error","error":"…","errorInfo":{…}}. Splat jobs return vspUrl and stats: {splats, chunks} instead. signed: true means the artifact carries an Ed25519 signature the browser verifies against /v1/pubkey.

3. Share. url is the ready-to-open walkthrough. Embed it with the SDK (docs/embed-sdk.md) or an iframe. Scenes uploaded with an account token are kept; anonymous ones are kept best-effort and the least-recently-opened are removed when the server's disk budget fills (Retention).

Publishing extras#

EndpointBodyReturns
POST /v1/experienceJSON {scene, …} per experience-format, ≤128 KB{path, url} — a ?experience= link
POST /v1/tourJSON {scene, samples:[[t,x,y,z,fx,fy,fz]×2..6000]}, ≤512 KB{path, url} — a ?tour= link
POST /v1/posterraw PNG, ≤4 MB{path, url} — a poster image URL

Live presence (shared tours)#

  • GET /v1/room/<id>/events — Server-Sent Events roster stream (id = [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}).
  • POST /v1/room/<id>/pose — JSON {id, name, color:"#rrggbb", pose:[x,y,z,fx,fy,fz]} ≤2 KB, ~8 Hz. Peers expire after 10 s of silence; 32 peers per room. Rooms are ephemeral, in-memory, unauthenticated — treat room ids as capability URLs.

Large files: resumable upload#

Above ~100 MB, use the resumable flow so an edge hiccup resumes instead of restarting: POST /v1/ingest/begin {size, name} → {uploadId}, ordered PUT /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId> with Content-Range, then POST /v1/ingest/commit/<uploadId> → the same 202 {job}. An out-of-order part answers 409 with the server's received offset to resume from. Details: Resumable uploads.

Own, protect, review#

  • POST /v1/account {name} → a token (shown once) that owns what you upload with Authorization: Bearer <token>: permanent scenes, /studio, analytics.
  • PATCH /v1/scenes/<id> {"visibility":"private"} + POST /v1/scenes/<id>/share → per-recipient share tokens; ?share=<token> on the link. Guide.
  • POST /v1/review/<id> {pos, text} / GET /v1/review/<id> — comments pinned in 3D on the shared scene. Guide.

Errors#

Every error the app generates is JSON {"error":"…"} with a real status and the header X-Verse-Error: 1: 401 unknown key, 404 unknown job, 409 out-of-order part, 413 body too large, 429 rate/quota, 503 compile queue full, 507 storage full. An error without the header came from the network edge, not the app — that one is worth a retry. Back off on 429/503; re-upload on error. Full rule: Error contract.

Building a plugin (Blender / Unity / Unreal)#

An exporter needs exactly three calls: export the scene to GLB, POST /v1/ingest (or the resumable trio), poll GET /v1/ingest/<job>, then hand the user the url. The shipped integrations are the reference implementations: integrations/blender/verse_publish (Extensions add-on, stdlib-only, verified in Blender 5.0.1), integrations/unity/com.ctruh.verse-publish (UPM package, verified in Unity 6000.6.5f1) and integrations/unreal/VersePublish (editor plugin, verified in Unreal Engine 5.8.3). Each has a README and a how-to guide; the server URL is configurable, so they work against the hosted service or a self-hosted origin identically. Minimal single-file protocol examples remain under tools/verselink-*.

/embed-sdk.html:
Reference

Embed SDK reference#

The Verse Embed SDK is one script, embed.js, served from the Verse origin. It mounts the engine in an iframe from our origin (the engine needs COOP/COEP for SharedArrayBuffer; your page needs no header changes), exposes a small typed API, and reports everything that happens as events. This page is generated from the typed contract in verse-embed.d.ts; the .d.ts is the source of truth and ships next to embed.js.

<!-- one line -->
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js" data-scene="SCENE_ID"></script>

<!-- or programmatic -->
<div id="viewer"></div>
<script src="https://HOST/embed.js"></script>
<script>
  const viewer = Verse.embed(document.getElementById("viewer"), { scene: "SCENE_ID" });
  viewer.on("loaded", (d) => console.log(d.clusters, "clusters"));
  const hit = await viewer.pick(0.5, 0.5);
</script>

Degradation ladder, every step telemetered: iframe + WebGPU (tier A/B) → iframe + WebGL2 (tier C) → poster + link-out (degraded event). Tier C streams the same scenes without the post chain; Gaussian splats need WebGPU. All scene URLs are resolved on the Verse origin — the engine never fetches bytes from a foreign host.

Loading the script#

AttributeEffect
data-scene="<id>"auto-mounts and loads ingest/<id>.vpk (a share link's scene id)
data-vpk="<url>"auto-mounts a streamed .vpk by URL
data-model="<url>"auto-mounts a .glb/.gltf/.splat/.ply, fetched whole
data-poster="<url>"image shown before the engine arrives, and on fallback
data-quality="4k"temporal super-resolution on tiers that support it
data-render="continuous"opt out of on-demand rendering (embeds default to demand — see the render option)
data-hdr="auto"opt in to HDR display output (embeds default to SDR — see the hdr option)
data-bg="0b0d12"solid backdrop in your page's colour instead of the studio environment (see the bg option)
data-target="<css selector>"mount into that element instead of the script's parent

With any of data-scene / data-vpk / data-model the SDK mounts immediately and exposes the viewer as window.Verse.instance. Without them nothing happens until you call Verse.embed().

<verse-viewer>: the same script also defines a custom element — <verse-viewer src="<scene id>" poster="…" autoplay-tour></verse-viewer> — lazy, responsive, with DOM events (load, progress, error, hotspot, view-change) and setCamera() / playTour() / screenshot(). autoplay-path (or Verse.embed(el, { autoplayPath: true }), or ?autoplay=path on a share link) plays the scene's default camera path — its automatic walkthrough / fly-through, or the owner's edit of it — as soon as it opens. Attributes, events and React / Vue wrappers: developers.md. Options it adds to Verse.embed() too: tier ("a" | "c"), aspect ("16:9" … or "fill"), engaged (scroll guard starts engaged), onEvent(type, detail); and viewer.destroy() unmounts.

Verse.embed(target, options)#

Mounts a viewer into target (an HTMLElement) and returns a VerseViewer. The mount is a div.verse-embed filling the target's width at a 16:9 aspect ratio; style it with CSS.

VerseEmbedOptions#

OptionTypeMeaning
scenestringingest scene id — loads ingest/<scene>.vpk from the Verse origin
vpkstringfull or relative URL to a streamed .vpk
modelstringURL to a .glb/.gltf (or .splat/.ply), fetched whole — small scenes, classic mode
glbstring(2.8) a Fidelity mode scene — ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb from the job record's glbUrl — opened on the reference-grade classic path: exact textures, studio lighting, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, both tiers
lookstring(2.8) with glb: the studio preset and backdrop, studio:neutral|warm|dark[,bg:rrggbb] (the look the upload chose; bg below still wins)
posterstringposter image shown before the engine arrives (and on fallback)
quality"4k"enables temporal super-resolution on tiers that support it
analyticsbooleancollect events into viewer.events() (default true). false also keeps the viewer's look-and-stall analytics feed off (2.5: no position samples leave the iframe)
variantstringConfigurator (2.5): open on a named material variant of the scene's KHR_materials_variants table (same as setVariant after load)
lightsstring | VerseLightsStateLight studio (2.7): open with a look — the ?lights= string a share link carries, or a state object (same as setLights after load)
exterior{ sky?, weather?, fog?, ground? }Exterior kit (2.7): open with a look — the share-string knobs as the viewer writes them (sky: "3,1,0.4,0.6", weather: "rain,0.7,2", fog: "0.02,0,8fa3bf,0.2", ground: "grass,60"); use setExterior after load for the object form
cinematicbooleanCinematic stills (2.7): path-trace the frame whenever the camera is still (WebGPU tiers; WebGL2 keeps the raster and the cinematic event says refusal: 7). Default false
cfgstring | { group: option }Configurator depth (2.7): open on a configuration from the owner's schema — the ?cfg= string (fabric:oak,legs:black) or an object (same as setConfiguration after load)
render"demand" | "continuous"frame scheduling; embeds default to "demand" — the engine renders only while something changes (camera, tours, animations, streaming, peers) and parks otherwise, so a still viewer costs the host page ~zero battery. "continuous" restores the classic every-vsync loop
bgstringWhat sits behind the model (2.8 forms): "#rrggbb" paints one solid colour (exact; the studio environment still lights the model); "transparent" draws nothing so your page shows through; "grad:rrggbb,rrggbb" a vertical gradient; "studio:neutral" / "studio:warm" / "studio:dark" a studio environment as the backdrop (and the lighting); "image:ingest/<id>.bg.jpg" / "hdr:ingest/<id>.bg.hdr" the scene owner's uploaded backdrop. Omit for the default (the owner's saved background, else the environment). Every tier. A gradient, picture or transparent opens the canvas with an alpha surface — set it here rather than only later through setBackground
hdr"auto" | 1 | 0HDR display output. Embeds default to SDR so the host page's colors never shift uninvited. "auto" uses the float16 extended-range swapchain when the display reports dynamic-range: high and the device is tier A; 1 forces it; 0 (default) pins SDR
reviewbooleanClient review pins: the "click a spot, leave a note" workflow, rendered inside the iframe. Default false — opt in per embed (data-review="1" on the auto-mount tag). See Client review pins in embeds
sharestringcapability token (32 hex chars) for a private scene — same token as the playground's ?share= link. Required for scene/vpk/model on a private scene, and for review: true on one
hotspotsbooleanOwner-authored hotspots + guided tour (2.7): numbered pins, info cards and a "Play tour" control from the scene's default experience (set in the Author bar / Studio) or a loaded .verse.json. Default true; false (data-hotspots="0") keeps the layer off and makes playTour() a no-op
guardbooleanguest manners, default true: vertical swipes and the mouse wheel scroll the host page until the visitor taps / clicks into the scene; false gives the scene every gesture from the start (?guard=0)
fullscreenbooleanthe fullscreen button, default true; on iPhone it opens the full viewer in a new tab (no Fullscreen API inside frames there). false hides it (?fs=0)

Give exactly one of scene / vpk / model, or none and call viewer.load() later (for example with an experience manifest).

const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { vpk: "ingest/scene.vpk", poster: "poster.jpg", quality: "4k" });

VerseViewer verbs#

Every verb posts a message into the engine iframe; none of them throw, and verbs sent before the engine is ready are simply not delivered — attach to ready first when timing matters.

element#

The mount element (div.verse-embed) the iframe lives in — remove it to tear the viewer down.

load(url)#

Load a scene. .vpk streams; .glb/.gltf and .splat/.ply fetch whole; a .verse.json experience manifest composes scene + props + ambience; a .tour.json recorded tour loads its scene and replays the camera path (a tour event fires when playback starts). All same origin. Replaces whatever is loaded.

viewer.on("ready", () => viewer.load("samples/experience-test.verse.json"));

camera({ orbit?, zoom? })#

Nudge the camera: orbit is [dx, dy] in pixels, zoom a scale factor.

viewer.camera({ orbit: [40, 0] });   // turn 40 px worth
viewer.camera({ zoom: 0.9 });        // move in 10 %

setCamera({ position, target? })#

Place the orbit camera: eye at position, orbiting and facing target (default the origin), world metres. Stops a playing tour and leaves walk mode; the visitor's drag continues from there. A view-change event ({ position, forward }, ≤ 4 Hz, only when the camera moved) reports where the camera is — after this call, and whenever the visitor moves.

viewer.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] });
viewer.on("view-change", ({ position }) => console.log(position));

screenshot(opts?)#

The current frame as a PNG Blob — saveStill() with the "viewport" preset unless opts.preset says otherwise.

walk(on)#

First-person walk mode on/off. Collision walk over the scene's occupancy grid; the visitor uses WASD / arrows, a joystick on touch.

viewer.walk(true);

move({ forward?, strafe?, up? })#

Analog walk vector, each component in [-1, 1] — drive walk mode from your own joystick or gamepad.

gamepadLoop(() => viewer.move({ forward: -pad.axes[1], strafe: pad.axes[0] }));

setDepthOfField(focus, aperture)#

Cinematic depth of field: focus distance in metres, aperture in px·m; aperture 0 disables. Tiers A/B, non-temporal mode only.

viewer.setDepthOfField(3.5, 12);
viewer.setDepthOfField(0, 0); // off

addEmitter({ kind, position, scale? }) / clearEmitters()#

Preset GPU particle emitter at a world position (tier A/B). kind is "fire" | "smoke" | "fountain" | "dust".

viewer.addEmitter({ kind: "fire", position: [0, 0.2, -2], scale: 1.5 });
viewer.clearEmitters();

spawnProp(opts) / throwProp(opts?) / clearProps()#

Dynamic rigid props: a ball or box that falls, bounces and collides with the scene. glTF scenes only — a prop event with id: -1 means the scene cannot draw props.

FieldspawnPropthrowPropMeaning
shape"ball" | "box"samedefault "ball"
position[x, y, z]—spawn point (default [0, 1, 0])
velocity[x, y, z]—initial velocity
speed—numberm/s along the view direction (default 8)
sizenumbernumberradius / half-extent in metres (default 0.15)
color[r, g, b][r, g, b]0–1
viewer.spawnProp({ shape: "box", position: [0.4, 2, 0], size: 0.15, color: [1, 0.4, 0.2] });
viewer.throwProp({ speed: 10 });
viewer.clearProps();

goTo(id)#

Jump to a hotspot of the loaded experience manifest. Enters walk mode at the hotspot's position facing its look target; emits hotspot.

viewer.on("experience", (x) => buildButtons(x.hotspots, (h) => viewer.goTo(h.id)));

stopTour()#

Stop a playing recorded tour (.tour.json) or the owner's guided tour (2.7); input returns to the viewer. Recorded tours start via load("….tour.json") and announce themselves with the tour event.

viewer.on("tour", (t) => showSkipButton(() => viewer.stopTour()));

playTour()#

Play the owner's guided tour (2.7): the camera flies between the recorded steps (~2 m/s, at least 1.2 s a leg), rests dwell seconds at each while that step's narration (text + optional audio clip) shows inside the iframe, and ends with the walker standing at the last step. Events: tour { playing: true, steps } at the start, tour-step per step, tour { playing: false, completed } at the end. Without a tour (or with hotspots: false) it only emits tour { playing: false, steps: 0 }.

viewer.on("hotspots", (h) => (playBtn.hidden = h.tour === 0));
playBtn.onclick = () => viewer.playTour();
viewer.on("tour-step", (s) => caption.textContent = `${s.step + 1} / ${s.of}`);

autoLook(opts?) / undoAutoLook()#

Auto look (2.7.2): "Make it look good" in one call — the best first view (composition-scored over the auto tour's waypoints and the room's centre), exposure, a sampled sun, fill and soft shadows, the physical sky for exteriors, every quality knob the tier has (SSAO, SSR, glass; Cinematic on WebGPU when the traced frame agrees with the raster look) and the walkthrough. Resolves a VerseAutoLookResult: before / after (median, p5, p95), view, composition, sun + sunSamples, ev / env / all / soft, sky, quality, walkthrough and lights — the ?lights= string to put in a link. The same object arrives as an auto-look event; auto-look-step reports each step. { walkthrough: false } lights without starting the tour; { replay: true } applies what the iframe URL carries and walks. Baked scenes get exposure and the quality knobs only. undoAutoLook() restores the state before the call. See the guide: make-it-look-good.md.

const look = await viewer.autoLook();
shareLink.search = `?scene=…&lights=${encodeURIComponent(look.lights)}&auto=1`;
viewer.on("auto-look-step", (s) => (progress.textContent = s.name));

setSun(azimuth, elevation, intensity?)#

Time-of-day sun: azimuth/elevation in degrees, intensity (default 2.8). Shadows and shading move together.

viewer.setSun(120, 15, 2.0);   // late-afternoon light from the south-east

setExposure(ev)#

Exposure control: EV stops applied in linear space before the tonemap, clamped to ±4. 0 is the default look. Pass "auto" for a one-shot scene-adaptive nudge that measures the current frame and lands its average luminance near mid-gray (clamped ±2 EV, never continuous — dark-authored scans brighten once, with no visible pumping). Auto is a no-op on tier C (WebGL2 has no readback path); manual EVs work on every tier. The playground's URL twin is ?exposure=<ev> / ?exposure=auto.

viewer.setExposure(1.5);      // +1.5 EV — lift a dark-textured scan
viewer.setExposure("auto");   // measure once, land near mid-gray

setClipPlanes(planes, opts?)#

Inspection (2.7): section cuts. Up to six world-space clip planes, each [nx, ny, nz, d] or { normal, distance }; a surface point stays iff dot(normal, p) + distance >= 0. Geometry on the cut side is discarded per fragment and its clusters are culled (nothing is streamed for what a cut removes); the faces the cut reveals fill with opts.cap (sRGB hex, default terracotta #e8734a). Six axis-aligned planes with inward normals make a section box. Streamed (.vpk) scenes only — classic GLB meshes are not clipped; an empty list restores the uncut view. The playground's URL twin is ?clip=. Fires a clip event with the live count.

viewer.setClipPlanes([[0, -1, 0, 1.2]]);                 // take the roof off: keep y ≤ 1.2
viewer.setClipPlanes([{ normal: [1, 0, 0], distance: -2.5 }], { cap: "#ffb000" });
viewer.setClipPlanes([]);                                // uncut

measure(mode, opts?)#

Inspection (2.7): the measure tool inside the iframe. "distance" (two taps), "polyline" (taps, Enter to finish) or "area" (corners, Enter to close) turn clean clicks into surface-snapped points (the GPU pick plus its normal); the viewer draws the lines, points and a dimension label. measure events report every tap (complete: false) and each finished measurement (complete: true, value in metres or square metres, label formatted in opts.units — "m", "cm" or "ftin"). "off" ends the mode, "clear" removes the drawn measurements; Escape cancels the one in progress. Turning the tool on takes the clicks away from review mode.

viewer.measure("distance", { units: "ftin" });
viewer.on("measure", (m) => { if (m.complete) console.log(m.label, m.points); });

enterAR()#

"See it in your room" (2.7, guide): open the scene in AR on a phone — a WebXR AR session (Android Chrome: hit-test reticle, tap to place, one finger turns, pinch scales, light estimation) or iOS AR Quick Look (the scene's .usdz), whichever the device has. The viewer shows its own View in AR control inside the frame for product-scale scenes; the stage event's ar field tells your page which path applies ("webxr", "quicklook" or null — not product-scale, or no AR here), and ar events report what happened. WebXR needs a user gesture inside the frame, so a programmatic enterAR() on Android may come back as ar { state: "blocked" }; wire your own button to it on iOS (Quick Look follows the link) and let the in-frame control do the rest.

viewer.on("stage", (s) => { if (s.ar) showYourArBadge(s.ar); });
viewer.on("ar", (e) => console.log(e.mode, e.state, e.scale ?? "", e.reason ?? ""));
yourButton.onclick = () => viewer.enterAR();

setMaterial(opts) / resetMaterials()#

Live material variant by glTF material index; omitted fields keep their current value. resetMaterials() restores the originals.

FieldTypeMeaning
indexnumbermaterial index (see pick().material)
baseColor[r, g, b, a?]0–1 albedo (alpha optional)
metallicnumber0–1
roughnessnumber0–1
emissive[r, g, b]emissive color
const hit = await viewer.pick(0.5, 0.5);
viewer.setMaterial({ index: hit.material, baseColor: [0.8, 0.2, 0.2] });
viewer.resetMaterials();

setVariant(name)#

Configurator (2.5): switch the scene's KHR_materials_variants by name; null restores the file's defaults. The variant names arrive on the stage event (detail.variants); the outcome comes back as a variant event (ok: false = unknown name, or the scene has no variants). Streamed scenes: the switch happens at the material table (every surface of the default material takes the variant material's colour and texture, in a frame, with no re-stream), on both GPU tiers. The link form is ?variant=<name>.

viewer.on("stage", (s) => renderSwatches(s.variants)); // ["Oak", "Walnut"]
viewer.setVariant("Walnut");
viewer.on("variant", (v) => console.log(v.name, v.ok));

setLights(state)#

Light studio (2.7): re-light the scene without a recompile, on both tiers. state is a ?lights= string or an object — all (every light, the sun and every emitter), env (image-based ambient), ev (exposure stops), soft (sun shadow penumbra, in shadow texels; also the path tracer's sun disc), sun: { az, el, intensity } (null = the scene's default), lights: { [index]: ×} per KHR_lights_punctual light and emissive: { [material]: ×} per emissive material. Multipliers are 0–16, 1 = as authored. The detected lights' names arrive on the stage event (detail.lights.punctual / .emissive, in the index order used here); the outcome comes back as a lights event with the full state and the share-link query. WebGL2 honours everything except per-light multipliers on streamed scenes (its streamed raster has no punctual lights).

viewer.on("stage", (s) => renderLightRows(s.lights.punctual, s.lights.emissive));
viewer.setLights({ all: 1.2, env: 0.6, emissive: { 3: 2 } });
viewer.on("lights", (l) => (shareLink.search = `?scene=…&lights=${encodeURIComponent(l.query)}`));

setExterior(state) / getExterior()#

Exterior kit (2.7), both tiers: a physical sky (Preetham daylight driven by setSun, turbidity, exposure, a procedural cloud layer — or model: "atmosphere", a single-scattering clear sky that also warms the sun, with aerial: 1 for clear-air aerial perspective) that also feeds the ambient of live-lit surfaces, weather (rain or snow as a camera-anchored particle sheet; rain also wets upward-facing surfaces — WebGPU and WebGL2 streamed scenes), height fog, and a ground plane / heightfield around the model that the walker stands on. state is a nested partial patch (unmentioned fields keep their values), a full state, or null for everything off; the outcome comes back as an exterior event with the full state and the share-string query. getExterior() returns the last reported state (null before the first event). ground.heightfield is the scene's ingest/<id>.ground.png (uploaded with PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/ground — scenes.setGround in the JS SDK).

viewer.setSun(140, 25, 3);
viewer.setExterior({
  sky: { on: true, turbidity: 3, clouds: { coverage: 0.4 } },
  weather: { kind: "rain", intensity: 0.6, wind: [3, 0] },
  fog: { on: true, density: 0.015, height: 0, colour: "9fb0c8" },
  ground: { kind: "plane", material: "grass", size: 120 },
});
viewer.on("exterior", (e) => (shareLink.search = `?scene=…&sky=${e.query.sky}&weather=${e.query.weather}`));

setMedia(table) / getMedia() / setAudioMuted(muted)#

Media surfaces + spatial audio (2.7, streamed scenes, both tiers). A scene's owner-authored table (videos on surfaces, ambient sounds — guide) mounts on load; setMedia replaces it live without persisting (null clears): { media: [{ material, url, loop?, emissive?, audio? }], audio: [{ pos, url, radius?, loop?, gain? }] } with same-origin URLs (an /ingest/<id>.media/<n>.mp4 from the upload route, or any path on the viewer's origin). getMedia() is the table the viewer last reported. Screens play muted and loop; a screen pauses when it is behind the visitor or farther than 40 m and resumes in view; prefers-reduced-motion shows one poster frame. Sound (a screen's own track with audio: true, and the emitters) is positioned at the surface / the point and follows the camera, and starts only after a gesture inside the frame: the viewer's Sound chip is that gesture, setAudioMuted the same switch for the host page. Events: media (the table that mounted — surfaces[].bound says the material was found — and each play / pause with material, playing, visible; error per source) and audio (muted, emitters loaded / failed).

viewer.setMedia({ media: [{ material: 3, url: "/ingest/abc.media/1.mp4", emissive: 1.5, audio: true }], audio: [] });
viewer.on("media", (m) => m.material != null && console.log(`screen ${m.material} ${m.playing ? "playing" : "paused"}`));
soundButton.onclick = () => viewer.setAudioMuted(false);

setCinematic(on) / saveStill(opts?)#

Cinematic stills (2.7): with Cinematic on, a still camera on a lit streamed scene is path-traced progressively (global illumination, soft shadows, emissive area lights, glass) and converges in place; moving the camera returns to the raster instantly. cinematic events report the accumulation (active, samples, converged, or a refusal with its reason — 2 needs a streamed scene, 3 baked scene, 4 over the triangle budget, 5 several objects, 6 animating, 7 needs WebGPU). saveStill resolves { blob, width, height, spp, ms }: preset: "viewport" is the live frame (traced when Cinematic has converged, raster otherwise), "1080p" / "4k" a tiled path-traced export at that size (spp samples per pixel, default 64 — ~5 s for 1080p at 64 spp on a laptop GPU, 4K about four times that). One still at a time; the still event mirrors the summary.

viewer.setCinematic(true);
viewer.on("cinematic", (c) => (hud.textContent = c.active ? `${c.samples} spp` : c.reason));
const { blob } = await viewer.saveStill({ preset: "1080p", spp: 64 });

setConfiguration(selection)#

Configurator depth (2.7): pick options by group from the owner's configuration schema ({ fabric: "oak" }, merged onto the current pick — groups you omit keep theirs). The schema arrives on the first configuration event after load (detail.groups: ids, names, options with swatch/price/SKU); every change — this call, ?cfg=, the panel in a full viewer — emits another one with the selection, the cfg string for a share link, the price total (display only) and the SKUs. ok: false on the event means a group or option you named does not exist (the rest was applied). A scene without a schema has groups: [] and the call is a no-op. Build your own swatches from the event and keep the viewer headless, or just open with cfg.

viewer.on("configuration", (c) => {
  renderGroups(c.groups, c.selection);          // your UI
  priceEl.textContent = c.priced ? `${c.total} ${c.currency}` : "";
  shareLink.search = c.cfg ? `?cfg=${c.cfg}` : "";
});
viewer.setConfiguration({ fabric: "walnut", legs: "none" });

getConfiguration() → Promise<VerseConfiguration>#

The current pick in the same shape as the configuration event.

joinRoom(room, { voice?, name? }) / leaveRoom() / follow(id)#

Live tours: join a named presence room — every viewer in the room sees the others as in-world avatars, and the roster arrives as presence events. follow(id) glues the camera to a viewer from the roster; follow(null) stops following. Poses are ephemeral on the server (memory-only, 10 s TTL). The older joinRoom({ room, name }) form still works.

Voice (2.7). voice: true (open mic) or "ptt" (push-to-talk) joins the room's peer-to-peer audio: the browser asks for the microphone, each talker holds one WebRTC connection per other talker (a mesh — **6 talkers per room**, the seventh gets a room notice and no audio), signalling rides the room's SSE stream and POST /v1/room/<room>/signal, STUN only (no TURN: a pair behind symmetric NATs gets a room notice instead of audio). Nothing is recorded and no audio reaches the server. Playback is spatial — each voice sits where its avatar stands — until setVoice({ spatial: false }).

viewer.joinRoom("showflat-42", { name: "Alex", voice: true });
viewer.on("room", (r) => r.state === "voice-failed" && toast(r.message));
viewer.on("speaking", (s) => roster.mark(s.id, s.speaking));
viewer.on("peer", (p) => p.state === "hand" && toast(`${p.name} raised a hand`));
viewer.setVoice({ muted: true });              // or { pushToTalk: true, talking: held }
viewer.setVoice({ peer: someId, peerMuted: true }); // for me only
viewer.leaveRoom();

present(on?) / setVoice(opts)#

Presenter mode (2.7). present(true) takes the floor: everyone else in the room follows your camera (smoothed) behind an in-frame veil with Take control and Raise hand buttons, and your playTour() / stopTour() / goTo() / setVariant() / setLights() / setClipPlanes() calls are broadcast and applied on every follower. Your pick point is drawn for them as a laser dot. present(false) gives the floor back; a second viewer calling present(true) takes it over (the previous presenter is told through a room event). The roster's peer.flags.presenter / hand / muted say who is who.

setVoice({ on?, muted?, pushToTalk?, talking?, spatial?, peer?, peerMuted? }) drives the voice knobs; on: false leaves voice, on: true joins it later than joinRoom.

addSound(opts) / clearSounds()#

Positioned ambience (HRTF): a synthesized kind ("fire" | "water" | "wind") or an audio url (CORS-readable), at position; optional gain, refDistance, loop. Audio starts on the visitor's first gesture, as browsers require.

viewer.addSound({ kind: "water", position: [2, 0, -1], gain: 0.6 });
viewer.addSound({ url: "/audio/loop.mp3", position: [0, 2, 0], loop: true });

play(clip?) / pause() / seek(t) / setSpeed(speed)#

Animation. Clips are listed by index on the loaded event's animations; the first clip auto-plays. seek takes seconds within the current clip; a negative speed plays backwards.

viewer.on("loaded", (d) => {
  console.log(d.animations); // ["Idle", "Wave"]
  viewer.play(1);
  viewer.setSpeed(0.5);
});

pick(x, y) → Promise<VersePickResult>#

GPU pick at normalized viewport coordinates ([0, 1], y down). Resolves with { hit, position, material, cluster }; hit is false on sky / outside geometry. Rejects after 5 s if the engine never answers (tier C). Also delivered as a pick event.

const r = await viewer.pick(0.5, 0.5);
if (r.hit) console.log("material", r.material, "at", r.position);

setBackground(bg) / getBackground() → Promise<string>#

(2.8) The background spec in effect — the same forms as the bg option. setBackground("transparent") on an embed that opened with a solid or default backdrop asks for an alpha canvas the frame does not have: the background event then says reload: true and the frame keeps its current backdrop — open the embed with bg set for those. Emits background { bg }.

viewer.setBackground("ffffff");              // exact white
viewer.setBackground("studio:dark");          // dark-contrast studio, lights the model
console.log(await viewer.getBackground());    // "studio:dark"

setEnvironment(src, name?) → Promise<void>#

Swap the lighting environment for a Radiance .hdr — an ArrayBuffer or a URL (fetched by the host page, so it may be cross-origin if CORS allows). Emits environment.

await viewer.setEnvironment("/env/evening.hdr");

exportVideo(opts?) → Promise<VerseExportResult> / cancelExport()#

Export video: records the scene's tour — the compile-time staged tour when the scene has one, otherwise a synthesized orbit of the framing sphere — to MP4/H.264 where the browser can mux it, WebM elsewhere. The capture runs inside the engine iframe (that is where the canvas lives); the finished bytes transfer to your page as a Blob, so the embedding page decides download/upload/preview. One export at a time — a second call rejects with "an export is already running"; so does an export before any scene loaded. export-progress events fire per captured frame; cancelExport() resolves the pending promise with { cancelled: true }.

OptionDefaultMeaning
durationtour lengthseconds, clamped 1–600
fps30clamped 5–60
height1080output height px; 0 = native canvas height
formatauto (MP4 where supported)"mp4" | "webm"
bitrate~10 Mbps at 1080p, area-scaledvideo bits/s

Resolves { blob, mimeType, name, width, height, frames, cancelled }.

viewer.on("export-progress", (p) => (bar.style.width = `${p.percent}%`));
const r = await viewer.exportVideo({ duration: 10, height: 1080 });
if (!r.cancelled) {
  const a = Object.assign(document.createElement("a"), {
    href: URL.createObjectURL(r.blob),
    download: r.name,
  });
  a.click();
}

setReviewMode(on) / getComments() → Promise<VerseReviewComment[]>#

Client review pins (embed parity): see Client review pins in embeds below. setReviewMode(on) toggles the "click a spot, leave a note" workflow inside the iframe — a no-op when the embed was not created with review: true (no review machinery exists in the iframe at all). getComments() resolves the current comment list for the loaded scene ([] when review was never enabled, or nothing has been posted yet).

getProperties(id?) / setVisible(ids, visible?) / isolate(ids) / select(id, { frame? })#

Object properties (2.7) on scenes that came in as IFC or USD (see docs/api.md → IFC and USD). getProperties(id) resolves one object by IFC GlobalId / USD prim path / glTF node index — { node, id, type, name, storey?, description?, tag?, props, bounds?, visible } — or null; with no argument it resolves the whole index ({ count, source, storeys, types, nodes }), or null on a scene without properties. setVisible(ids, false) hides objects (both tiers; hidden objects are dropped before the renderer's visibility test), setVisible("all") shows everything, isolate(ids) keeps only those. select(id) fires a select event like a click would; { frame: true } orbits the camera onto the object; select(null) clears.

const index = await viewer.getProperties();
viewer.setVisible(index.storeys.find((s) => s.name === "Level 2").nodes, false);
viewer.on("select", ({ object }) => render(object));

on(type, fn) → VerseViewer#

Subscribe to an event; chainable. **Already-emitted events are replayed to late listeners**, so attaching after ready fired still delivers it.

events()#

Every event captured so far, as Array<{ type, t, …detail }> — the analytics feed (disable capture with analytics: false).

viewer

  .on("progress", (p) => hud.bar.style.width = `${(100 * p.drawn) / p.total}%`)
  .on("dwell",    (d) => analytics.track("3d-dwell", { ms: d.ms }))
  .on("signed",   (s) => badge.hidden = s.signed !== true)
  .on("error",    (e) => console.warn("verse:", e.message));

FieldTypeMeaning

Client review pins in embeds#

Client review is available inside the embed SDK, default off. Set review: true (or data-review="1" on the auto-mount script tag) and a viewer gets the exact same "click a spot, leave a note" workflow the playground has — rendered inside the iframe, over your scene, no playground chrome involved:

  • A viewer toggles review mode with viewer.setReviewMode(true) (there is no built-in chip/button in the embed — that is the host page's UI to build, same as walk mode).
  • While on, a clean click/tap does a GPU pick and opens a small composer at that spot; posting pins a numbered marker and fires review-posted.
  • Existing pins render as the same numbered DOM markers the playground uses, projected from the camera pose each frame; clicking one opens its detail popover and fires review-selected.
  • The composer/detail popover clamps to the iframe's own bounds and scrolls internally if it would overflow — it fits down to a 320px-wide embed.
  • viewer.getComments() reads the current list without opening the UI — handy for a host-side counter/list.

Auth: embed comments are anonymous by default — only the optional free-text "your name" field identifies an author, there is no signed-in viewer concept in an embed. A private scene needs the same share token as loading the scene itself; pass it once and both the scene bytes and the review reads/posts use it:

const viewer = Verse.embed(el, {
  vpk: "ingest/scene.vpk",
  share: "a1b2…32 hex chars…",
  review: true,
});
viewer.on("ready", () => viewer.setReviewMode(true));
viewer.on("review-posted", (d) => console.log("new pin", d.id, d.pos, d.text));

Not in embeds: owner moderation (resolve/delete, the "show resolved" toggle's underlying data, the open/total counts on /v1/account/scenes) stays playground/studio-only — an embed viewer, even the scene's own owner browsing their own page, only ever sees the anonymous composer. Moderate from the playground or studio instead. See the parity table in api.md.

TypeScript#

import type { VerseViewer, VerseEventMap } from "./verse-embed";
declare const viewer: VerseViewer;
viewer.on("loaded", (d) => d.clusters); // d: VerseEventMap["loaded"]

verse-embed.d.ts declares window.Verse: VerseGlobal (embed() and the optional auto-mounted instance). Copy it into your project or reference it from the Verse origin.

Ingest from JavaScript#

Uploading is a separate, tiny module — verse-sdk.js wraps POST /v1/ingest and the job polling, then mounts the result:

import { VerseClient } from "https://HOST/verse-sdk.js";
const verse = new VerseClient({ endpoint: "https://HOST", apiKey: "vk_…" });
const { url } = await verse.ingest(glbArrayBuffer, { name: "chair" });
verse.mount(document.querySelector("#viewer"), url);

Protocol details: Ingest API.
