/embed-sdk.text:
REFERENCE Embed SDK reference# The Verse Embed SDK is one script, embed.js, served from the Verse origin. It mounts the engine in an iframe from our origin (the engine needs COOP/COEP for SharedArrayBuffer; your page needs no header changes), exposes a small typed API, and reports everything that happens as events. This page is generated from the typed contract in verse-embed.d.ts; the .d.ts is the source of truth and ships next to embed.js. Copy
Degradation ladder, every step telemetered: iframe + WebGPU (tier A/B) → iframe + WebGL2 (tier C) → poster + link-out (degraded event). Tier C streams the same scenes without the post chain; Gaussian splats need WebGPU. All scene URLs are resolved on the Verse origin — the engine never fetches bytes from a foreign host. Loading the script# Attribute Effect data-scene="" auto-mounts and loads ingest/.vpk (a share link's scene id) data-vpk="" auto-mounts a streamed .vpk by URL data-model="" auto-mounts a .glb/.gltf/.splat/.ply, fetched whole data-poster="" image shown before the engine arrives, and on fallback data-quality="4k" temporal super-resolution on tiers that support it data-render="continuous" opt out of on-demand rendering (embeds default to demand — see the render option) data-hdr="auto" opt in to HDR display output (embeds default to SDR — see the hdr option) data-bg="0b0d12" solid backdrop in your page's colour instead of the studio environment (see the bg option) data-target="" mount into that element instead of the script's parent With any of data-scene / data-vpk / data-model the SDK mounts immediately and exposes the viewer as window.Verse.instance. Without them nothing happens until you call Verse.embed(). : the same script also defines a custom element — — lazy, responsive, with DOM events (load, progress, error, hotspot, view-change) and setCamera() / playTour() / screenshot(). autoplay-path (or Verse.embed(el, { autoplayPath: true }), or ?autoplay=path on a share link) plays the scene's default camera path — its automatic walkthrough / fly-through, or the owner's edit of it — as soon as it opens. Attributes, events and React / Vue wrappers: developers.md. Options it adds to Verse.embed() too: tier ("a" | "c"), aspect ("16:9" … or "fill"), engaged (scroll guard starts engaged), onEvent(type, detail); and viewer.destroy() unmounts. Verse.embed(target, options)# Mounts a viewer into target (an HTMLElement) and returns a VerseViewer. The mount is a div.verse-embed filling the target's width at a 16:9 aspect ratio; style it with CSS. VerseEmbedOptions# Option Type Meaning scene string ingest scene id — loads ingest/.vpk from the Verse origin vpk string full or relative URL to a streamed .vpk model string URL to a .glb/.gltf (or .splat/.ply), fetched whole — small scenes, classic mode glb string (2.8) a Fidelity mode scene — ingest/.fidelity.glb from the job record's glbUrl — opened on the reference-grade classic path: exact textures, studio lighting, Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapping, both tiers look string (2.8) with glb: the studio preset and backdrop, studio:neutral|warm|dark[,bg:rrggbb] (the look the upload chose; bg below still wins) poster string poster image shown before the engine arrives (and on fallback) quality "4k" enables temporal super-resolution on tiers that support it analytics boolean collect events into viewer.events() (default true). false also keeps the viewer's look-and-stall analytics feed off (2.5: no position samples leave the iframe) variant string Configurator (2.5): open on a named material variant of the scene's KHR_materials_variants table (same as setVariant after load) lights string | VerseLightsState Light studio (2.7): open with a look — the ?lights= string a share link carries, or a state object (same as setLights after load) exterior { sky?, weather?, fog?, ground? } Exterior kit (2.7): open with a look — the share-string knobs as the viewer writes them (sky: "3,1,0.4,0.6", weather: "rain,0.7,2", fog: "0.02,0,8fa3bf,0.2", ground: "grass,60"); use setExterior after load for the object form cinematic boolean Cinematic stills (2.7): path-trace the frame whenever the camera is still (WebGPU tiers; WebGL2 keeps the raster and the cinematic event says refusal: 7). Default false cfg string | { group: option } Configurator depth (2.7): open on a configuration from the owner's schema — the ?cfg= string (fabric:oak,legs:black) or an object (same as setConfiguration after load) render "demand" | "continuous" frame scheduling; embeds default to "demand" — the engine renders only while something changes (camera, tours, animations, streaming, peers) and parks otherwise, so a still viewer costs the host page ~zero battery. "continuous" restores the classic every-vsync loop bg string What sits behind the model (2.8 forms): "#rrggbb" paints one solid colour (exact; the studio environment still lights the model); "transparent" draws nothing so your page shows through; "grad:rrggbb,rrggbb" a vertical gradient; "studio:neutral" / "studio:warm" / "studio:dark" a studio environment as the backdrop (and the lighting); "image:ingest/.bg.jpg" / "hdr:ingest/.bg.hdr" the scene owner's uploaded backdrop. Omit for the default (the owner's saved background, else the environment). Every tier. A gradient, picture or transparent opens the canvas with an alpha surface — set it here rather than only later through setBackground hdr "auto" | 1 | 0 HDR display output. Embeds default to SDR so the host page's colors never shift uninvited. "auto" uses the float16 extended-range swapchain when the display reports dynamic-range: high and the device is tier A; 1 forces it; 0 (default) pins SDR review boolean Client review pins: the "click a spot, leave a note" workflow, rendered inside the iframe. Default false — opt in per embed (data-review="1" on the auto-mount tag). See Client review pins in embeds share string capability token (32 hex chars) for a private scene — same token as the playground's ?share= link. Required for scene/vpk/model on a private scene, and for review: true on one hotspots boolean Owner-authored hotspots + guided tour (2.7): numbered pins, info cards and a "Play tour" control from the scene's default experience (set in the Author bar / Studio) or a loaded .verse.json. Default true; false (data-hotspots="0") keeps the layer off and makes playTour() a no-op guard boolean guest manners, default true: vertical swipes and the mouse wheel scroll the host page until the visitor taps / clicks into the scene; false gives the scene every gesture from the start (?guard=0) fullscreen boolean the fullscreen button, default true; on iPhone it opens the full viewer in a new tab (no Fullscreen API inside frames there). false hides it (?fs=0) Give exactly one of scene / vpk / model, or none and call viewer.load() later (for example with an experience manifest). Copy const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { vpk: "ingest/scene.vpk", poster: "poster.jpg", quality: "4k" }); VerseViewer verbs# Every verb posts a message into the engine iframe; none of them throw, and verbs sent before the engine is ready are simply not delivered — attach to ready first when timing matters. element# The mount element (div.verse-embed) the iframe lives in — remove it to tear the viewer down. load(url)# Load a scene. .vpk streams; .glb/.gltf and .splat/.ply fetch whole; a .verse.json experience manifest composes scene + props + ambience; a .tour.json recorded tour loads its scene and replays the camera path (a tour event fires when playback starts). All same origin. Replaces whatever is loaded. Copy viewer.on("ready", () => viewer.load("samples/experience-test.verse.json")); camera({ orbit?, zoom? })# Nudge the camera: orbit is [dx, dy] in pixels, zoom a scale factor. Copy viewer.camera({ orbit: [40, 0] }); // turn 40 px worth viewer.camera({ zoom: 0.9 }); // move in 10 % setCamera({ position, target? })# Place the orbit camera: eye at position, orbiting and facing target (default the origin), world metres. Stops a playing tour and leaves walk mode; the visitor's drag continues from there. A view-change event ({ position, forward }, ≤ 4 Hz, only when the camera moved) reports where the camera is — after this call, and whenever the visitor moves. Copy viewer.setCamera({ position: [3, 2, 4], target: [0, 1, 0] }); viewer.on("view-change", ({ position }) => console.log(position)); screenshot(opts?)# The current frame as a PNG Blob — saveStill() with the "viewport" preset unless opts.preset says otherwise. walk(on)# First-person walk mode on/off. Collision walk over the scene's occupancy grid; the visitor uses WASD / arrows, a joystick on touch. Copy viewer.walk(true); move({ forward?, strafe?, up? })# Analog walk vector, each component in [-1, 1] — drive walk mode from your own joystick or gamepad. Copy gamepadLoop(() => viewer.move({ forward: -pad.axes[1], strafe: pad.axes[0] })); setDepthOfField(focus, aperture)# Cinematic depth of field: focus distance in metres, aperture in px·m; aperture 0 disables. Tiers A/B, non-temporal mode only. Copy viewer.setDepthOfField(3.5, 12); viewer.setDepthOfField(0, 0); // off addEmitter({ kind, position, scale? }) / clearEmitters()# Preset GPU particle emitter at a world position (tier A/B). kind is "fire" | "smoke" | "fountain" | "dust". Copy viewer.addEmitter({ kind: "fire", position: [0, 0.2, -2], scale: 1.5 }); viewer.clearEmitters(); spawnProp(opts) / throwProp(opts?) / clearProps()# Dynamic rigid props: a ball or box that falls, bounces and collides with the scene. glTF scenes only — a prop event with id: -1 means the scene cannot draw props. Field spawnProp throwProp Meaning shape "ball" | "box" same default "ball" position [x, y, z] — spawn point (default [0, 1, 0]) velocity [x, y, z] — initial velocity speed — number m/s along the view direction (default 8) size number number radius / half-extent in metres (default 0.15) color [r, g, b] [r, g, b] 0–1 Copy viewer.spawnProp({ shape: "box", position: [0.4, 2, 0], size: 0.15, color: [1, 0.4, 0.2] }); viewer.throwProp({ speed: 10 }); viewer.clearProps(); goTo(id)# Jump to a hotspot of the loaded experience manifest. Enters walk mode at the hotspot's position facing its look target; emits hotspot. Copy viewer.on("experience", (x) => buildButtons(x.hotspots, (h) => viewer.goTo(h.id))); stopTour()# Stop a playing recorded tour (.tour.json) or the owner's guided tour (2.7); input returns to the viewer. Recorded tours start via load("….tour.json") and announce themselves with the tour event. Copy viewer.on("tour", (t) => showSkipButton(() => viewer.stopTour())); playTour()# Play the owner's guided tour (2.7): the camera flies between the recorded steps (~2 m/s, at least 1.2 s a leg), rests dwell seconds at each while that step's narration (text + optional audio clip) shows inside the iframe, and ends with the walker standing at the last step. Events: tour { playing: true, steps } at the start, tour-step per step, tour { playing: false, completed } at the end. Without a tour (or with hotspots: false) it only emits tour { playing: false, steps: 0 }. Copy viewer.on("hotspots", (h) => (playBtn.hidden = h.tour === 0)); playBtn.onclick = () => viewer.playTour(); viewer.on("tour-step", (s) => caption.textContent = `${s.step + 1} / ${s.of}`); autoLook(opts?) / undoAutoLook()# Auto look (2.7.2): "Make it look good" in one call — the best first view (composition-scored over the auto tour's waypoints and the room's centre), exposure, a sampled sun, fill and soft shadows, the physical sky for exteriors, every quality knob the tier has (SSAO, SSR, glass; Cinematic on WebGPU when the traced frame agrees with the raster look) and the walkthrough. Resolves a VerseAutoLookResult: before / after (median, p5, p95), view, composition, sun + sunSamples, ev / env / all / soft, sky, quality, walkthrough and lights — the ?lights= string to put in a link. The same object arrives as an auto-look event; auto-look-step reports each step. { walkthrough: false } lights without starting the tour; { replay: true } applies what the iframe URL carries and walks. Baked scenes get exposure and the quality knobs only. undoAutoLook() restores the state before the call. See the guide: make-it-look-good.md. Copy const look = await viewer.autoLook(); shareLink.search = `?scene=…&lights=${encodeURIComponent(look.lights)}&auto=1`; viewer.on("auto-look-step", (s) => (progress.textContent = s.name)); setSun(azimuth, elevation, intensity?)# Time-of-day sun: azimuth/elevation in degrees, intensity (default 2.8). Shadows and shading move together. Copy viewer.setSun(120, 15, 2.0); // late-afternoon light from the south-east setExposure(ev)# Exposure control: EV stops applied in linear space before the tonemap, clamped to ±4. 0 is the default look. Pass "auto" for a one-shot scene-adaptive nudge that measures the current frame and lands its average luminance near mid-gray (clamped ±2 EV, never continuous — dark-authored scans brighten once, with no visible pumping). Auto is a no-op on tier C (WebGL2 has no readback path); manual EVs work on every tier. The playground's URL twin is ?exposure= / ?exposure=auto. Copy viewer.setExposure(1.5); // +1.5 EV — lift a dark-textured scan viewer.setExposure("auto"); // measure once, land near mid-gray setClipPlanes(planes, opts?)# Inspection (2.7): section cuts. Up to six world-space clip planes, each [nx, ny, nz, d] or { normal, distance }; a surface point stays iff dot(normal, p) + distance >= 0. Geometry on the cut side is discarded per fragment and its clusters are culled (nothing is streamed for what a cut removes); the faces the cut reveals fill with opts.cap (sRGB hex, default terracotta #e8734a). Six axis-aligned planes with inward normals make a section box. Streamed (.vpk) scenes only — classic GLB meshes are not clipped; an empty list restores the uncut view. The playground's URL twin is ?clip=. Fires a clip event with the live count. Copy viewer.setClipPlanes([[0, -1, 0, 1.2]]); // take the roof off: keep y ≤ 1.2 viewer.setClipPlanes([{ normal: [1, 0, 0], distance: -2.5 }], { cap: "#ffb000" }); viewer.setClipPlanes([]); // uncut measure(mode, opts?)# Inspection (2.7): the measure tool inside the iframe. "distance" (two taps), "polyline" (taps, Enter to finish) or "area" (corners, Enter to close) turn clean clicks into surface-snapped points (the GPU pick plus its normal); the viewer draws the lines, points and a dimension label. measure events report every tap (complete: false) and each finished measurement (complete: true, value in metres or square metres, label formatted in opts.units — "m", "cm" or "ftin"). "off" ends the mode, "clear" removes the drawn measurements; Escape cancels the one in progress. Turning the tool on takes the clicks away from review mode. Copy viewer.measure("distance", { units: "ftin" }); viewer.on("measure", (m) => { if (m.complete) console.log(m.label, m.points); }); enterAR()# "See it in your room" (2.7, guide): open the scene in AR on a phone — a WebXR AR session (Android Chrome: hit-test reticle, tap to place, one finger turns, pinch scales, light estimation) or iOS AR Quick Look (the scene's .usdz), whichever the device has. The viewer shows its own View in AR control inside the frame for product-scale scenes; the stage event's ar field tells your page which path applies ("webxr", "quicklook" or null — not product-scale, or no AR here), and ar events report what happened. WebXR needs a user gesture inside the frame, so a programmatic enterAR() on Android may come back as ar { state: "blocked" }; wire your own button to it on iOS (Quick Look follows the link) and let the in-frame control do the rest. Copy viewer.on("stage", (s) => { if (s.ar) showYourArBadge(s.ar); }); viewer.on("ar", (e) => console.log(e.mode, e.state, e.scale ?? "", e.reason ?? "")); yourButton.onclick = () => viewer.enterAR(); setMaterial(opts) / resetMaterials()# Live material variant by glTF material index; omitted fields keep their current value. resetMaterials() restores the originals. Field Type Meaning index number material index (see pick().material) baseColor [r, g, b, a?] 0–1 albedo (alpha optional) metallic number 0–1 roughness number 0–1 emissive [r, g, b] emissive color Copy const hit = await viewer.pick(0.5, 0.5); viewer.setMaterial({ index: hit.material, baseColor: [0.8, 0.2, 0.2] }); viewer.resetMaterials(); setVariant(name)# Configurator (2.5): switch the scene's KHR_materials_variants by name; null restores the file's defaults. The variant names arrive on the stage event (detail.variants); the outcome comes back as a variant event (ok: false = unknown name, or the scene has no variants). Streamed scenes: the switch happens at the material table (every surface of the default material takes the variant material's colour and texture, in a frame, with no re-stream), on both GPU tiers. The link form is ?variant=. Copy viewer.on("stage", (s) => renderSwatches(s.variants)); // ["Oak", "Walnut"] viewer.setVariant("Walnut"); viewer.on("variant", (v) => console.log(v.name, v.ok)); setLights(state)# Light studio (2.7): re-light the scene without a recompile, on both tiers. state is a ?lights= string or an object — all (every light, the sun and every emitter), env (image-based ambient), ev (exposure stops), soft (sun shadow penumbra, in shadow texels; also the path tracer's sun disc), sun: { az, el, intensity } (null = the scene's default), lights: { [index]: ×} per KHR_lights_punctual light and emissive: { [material]: ×} per emissive material. Multipliers are 0–16, 1 = as authored. The detected lights' names arrive on the stage event (detail.lights.punctual / .emissive, in the index order used here); the outcome comes back as a lights event with the full state and the share-link query. WebGL2 honours everything except per-light multipliers on streamed scenes (its streamed raster has no punctual lights). Copy viewer.on("stage", (s) => renderLightRows(s.lights.punctual, s.lights.emissive)); viewer.setLights({ all: 1.2, env: 0.6, emissive: { 3: 2 } }); viewer.on("lights", (l) => (shareLink.search = `?scene=…&lights=${encodeURIComponent(l.query)}`)); setExterior(state) / getExterior()# Exterior kit (2.7), both tiers: a physical sky (Preetham daylight driven by setSun, turbidity, exposure, a procedural cloud layer — or model: "atmosphere", a single-scattering clear sky that also warms the sun, with aerial: 1 for clear-air aerial perspective) that also feeds the ambient of live-lit surfaces, weather (rain or snow as a camera-anchored particle sheet; rain also wets upward-facing surfaces — WebGPU and WebGL2 streamed scenes), height fog, and a ground plane / heightfield around the model that the walker stands on. state is a nested partial patch (unmentioned fields keep their values), a full state, or null for everything off; the outcome comes back as an exterior event with the full state and the share-string query. getExterior() returns the last reported state (null before the first event). ground.heightfield is the scene's ingest/.ground.png (uploaded with PUT /v1/scenes//ground — scenes.setGround in the JS SDK). A scene's owner-authored table (videos on surfaces, ambient sounds — guide) mounts on load; setMedia replaces it live without persisting (null clears): { media: [{ material, url, loop?, emissive?, audio? }], audio: [{ pos, url, radius?, loop?, gain? }] } with same-origin URLs (an /ingest/.media/.mp4 from the upload route, or any path on the viewer's origin). getMedia() is the table the viewer last reported. Screens play muted and loop; a screen pauses when it is behind the visitor or farther than 40 m and resumes in view; prefers-reduced-motion shows one poster frame. Sound (a screen's own track with audio: true, and the emitters) is positioned at the surface / the point and follows the camera, and starts only after a gesture inside the frame: the viewer's Sound chip is that gesture, setAudioMuted the same switch for the host page. Events: media (the table that mounted — surfaces[].bound says the material was found — and each play / pause with material, playing, visible; error per source) and audio (muted, emitters loaded / failed). Copy viewer.setMedia({ media: [{ material: 3, url: "/ingest/abc.media/1.mp4", emissive: 1.5, audio: true }], audio: [] }); viewer.on("media", (m) => m.material != null && console.log(`screen ${m.material} ${m.playing ? "playing" : "paused"}`)); soundButton.onclick = () => viewer.setAudioMuted(false); setCinematic(on) / saveStill(opts?)# Cinematic stills (2.7): with Cinematic on, a still camera on a lit streamed scene is path-traced progressively (global illumination, soft shadows, emissive area lights, glass) and converges in place; moving the camera returns to the raster instantly. cinematic events report the accumulation (active, samples, converged, or a refusal with its reason — 2 needs a streamed scene, 3 baked scene, 4 over the triangle budget, 5 several objects, 6 animating, 7 needs WebGPU). saveStill resolves { blob, width, height, spp, ms }: preset: "viewport" is the live frame (traced when Cinematic has converged, raster otherwise), "1080p" / "4k" a tiled path-traced export at that size (spp samples per pixel, default 64 — ~5 s for 1080p at 64 spp on a laptop GPU, 4K about four times that). One still at a time; the still event mirrors the summary. Copy viewer.setCinematic(true); viewer.on("cinematic", (c) => (hud.textContent = c.active ? `${c.samples} spp` : c.reason)); const { blob } = await viewer.saveStill({ preset: "1080p", spp: 64 }); setConfiguration(selection)# Configurator depth (2.7): pick options by group from the owner's configuration schema ({ fabric: "oak" }, merged onto the current pick — groups you omit keep theirs). The schema arrives on the first configuration event after load (detail.groups: ids, names, options with swatch/price/SKU); every change — this call, ?cfg=, the panel in a full viewer — emits another one with the selection, the cfg string for a share link, the price total (display only) and the SKUs. ok: false on the event means a group or option you named does not exist (the rest was applied). A scene without a schema has groups: [] and the call is a no-op. Build your own swatches from the event and keep the viewer headless, or just open with cfg. Copy viewer.on("configuration", (c) => { renderGroups(c.groups, c.selection); // your UI priceEl.textContent = c.priced ? `${c.total} ${c.currency}` : ""; shareLink.search = c.cfg ? `?cfg=${c.cfg}` : ""; }); viewer.setConfiguration({ fabric: "walnut", legs: "none" }); getConfiguration() → Promise# The current pick in the same shape as the configuration event. joinRoom(room, { voice?, name? }) / leaveRoom() / follow(id)# Live tours: join a named presence room — every viewer in the room sees the others as in-world avatars, and the roster arrives as presence events. follow(id) glues the camera to a viewer from the roster; follow(null) stops following. Poses are ephemeral on the server (memory-only, 10 s TTL). The older joinRoom({ room, name }) form still works. Voice (2.7). voice: true (open mic) or "ptt" (push-to-talk) joins the room's peer-to-peer audio: the browser asks for the microphone, each talker holds one WebRTC connection per other talker (a mesh — **6 talkers per room**, the seventh gets a room notice and no audio), signalling rides the room's SSE stream and POST /v1/room//signal, STUN only (no TURN: a pair behind symmetric NATs gets a room notice instead of audio). Nothing is recorded and no audio reaches the server. Playback is spatial — each voice sits where its avatar stands — until setVoice({ spatial: false }). Copy viewer.joinRoom("showflat-42", { name: "Alex", voice: true }); viewer.on("room", (r) => r.state === "voice-failed" && toast(r.message)); viewer.on("speaking", (s) => roster.mark(s.id, s.speaking)); viewer.on("peer", (p) => p.state === "hand" && toast(`${p.name} raised a hand`)); viewer.setVoice({ muted: true }); // or { pushToTalk: true, talking: held } viewer.setVoice({ peer: someId, peerMuted: true }); // for me only viewer.leaveRoom(); present(on?) / setVoice(opts)# Presenter mode (2.7). present(true) takes the floor: everyone else in the room follows your camera (smoothed) behind an in-frame veil with Take control and Raise hand buttons, and your playTour() / stopTour() / goTo() / setVariant() / setLights() / setClipPlanes() calls are broadcast and applied on every follower. Your pick point is drawn for them as a laser dot. present(false) gives the floor back; a second viewer calling present(true) takes it over (the previous presenter is told through a room event). The roster's peer.flags.presenter / hand / muted say who is who. setVoice({ on?, muted?, pushToTalk?, talking?, spatial?, peer?, peerMuted? }) drives the voice knobs; on: false leaves voice, on: true joins it later than joinRoom. addSound(opts) / clearSounds()# Positioned ambience (HRTF): a synthesized kind ("fire" | "water" | "wind") or an audio url (CORS-readable), at position; optional gain, refDistance, loop. Audio starts on the visitor's first gesture, as browsers require. Copy viewer.addSound({ kind: "water", position: [2, 0, -1], gain: 0.6 }); viewer.addSound({ url: "/audio/loop.mp3", position: [0, 2, 0], loop: true }); play(clip?) / pause() / seek(t) / setSpeed(speed)# Animation. Clips are listed by index on the loaded event's animations; the first clip auto-plays. seek takes seconds within the current clip; a negative speed plays backwards. Copy viewer.on("loaded", (d) => { console.log(d.animations); // ["Idle", "Wave"] viewer.play(1); viewer.setSpeed(0.5); }); pick(x, y) → Promise# GPU pick at normalized viewport coordinates ([0, 1], y down). Resolves with { hit, position, material, cluster }; hit is false on sky / outside geometry. Rejects after 5 s if the engine never answers (tier C). Also delivered as a pick event. Copy const r = await viewer.pick(0.5, 0.5); if (r.hit) console.log("material", r.material, "at", r.position); setBackground(bg) / getBackground() → Promise# (2.8) The background spec in effect — the same forms as the bg option. setBackground("transparent") on an embed that opened with a solid or default backdrop asks for an alpha canvas the frame does not have: the background event then says reload: true and the frame keeps its current backdrop — open the embed with bg set for those. Emits background { bg }. Copy viewer.setBackground("ffffff"); // exact white viewer.setBackground("studio:dark"); // dark-contrast studio, lights the model console.log(await viewer.getBackground()); // "studio:dark" setEnvironment(src, name?) → Promise# Swap the lighting environment for a Radiance .hdr — an ArrayBuffer or a URL (fetched by the host page, so it may be cross-origin if CORS allows). Emits environment. Copy await viewer.setEnvironment("/env/evening.hdr"); exportVideo(opts?) → Promise / cancelExport()# Export video: records the scene's tour — the compile-time staged tour when the scene has one, otherwise a synthesized orbit of the framing sphere — to MP4/H.264 where the browser can mux it, WebM elsewhere. The capture runs inside the engine iframe (that is where the canvas lives); the finished bytes transfer to your page as a Blob, so the embedding page decides download/upload/preview. One export at a time — a second call rejects with "an export is already running"; so does an export before any scene loaded. export-progress events fire per captured frame; cancelExport() resolves the pending promise with { cancelled: true }. Option Default Meaning duration tour length seconds, clamped 1–600 fps 30 clamped 5–60 height 1080 output height px; 0 = native canvas height format auto (MP4 where supported) "mp4" | "webm" bitrate ~10 Mbps at 1080p, area-scaled video bits/s Resolves { blob, mimeType, name, width, height, frames, cancelled }. Copy viewer.on("export-progress", (p) => (bar.style.width = `${p.percent}%`)); const r = await viewer.exportVideo({ duration: 10, height: 1080 }); if (!r.cancelled) { const a = Object.assign(document.createElement("a"), { href: URL.createObjectURL(r.blob), download: r.name, }); a.click(); } setReviewMode(on) / getComments() → Promise# Client review pins (embed parity): see Client review pins in embeds below. setReviewMode(on) toggles the "click a spot, leave a note" workflow inside the iframe — a no-op when the embed was not created with review: true (no review machinery exists in the iframe at all). getComments() resolves the current comment list for the loaded scene ([] when review was never enabled, or nothing has been posted yet). getProperties(id?) / setVisible(ids, visible?) / isolate(ids) / select(id, { frame? })# Object properties (2.7) on scenes that came in as IFC or USD (see docs/api.md → IFC and USD). getProperties(id) resolves one object by IFC GlobalId / USD prim path / glTF node index — { node, id, type, name, storey?, description?, tag?, props, bounds?, visible } — or null; with no argument it resolves the whole index ({ count, source, storeys, types, nodes }), or null on a scene without properties. setVisible(ids, false) hides objects (both tiers; hidden objects are dropped before the renderer's visibility test), setVisible("all") shows everything, isolate(ids) keeps only those. select(id) fires a select event like a click would; { frame: true } orbits the camera onto the object; select(null) clears. Copy const index = await viewer.getProperties(); viewer.setVisible(index.storeys.find((s) => s.name === "Level 2").nodes, false); viewer.on("select", ({ object }) => render(object)); on(type, fn) → VerseViewer# Subscribe to an event; chainable. **Already-emitted events are replayed to late listeners**, so attaching after ready fired still delivers it. events()# Every event captured so far, as Array<{ type, t, …detail }> — the analytics feed (disable capture with analytics: false). Events (VerseEventMap)# Event Payload When ready { tier, ttfi } engine booted; tier is "A", "B" or "C", ttfi ms to first frame loaded { name, clusters?, streamed?, animations?, splats? } scene finished loading (streamed scenes keep refining afterwards); animations lists clip names for GLBs, splats the count for splat scenes progress { drawn, total } ~1 Hz streaming / culling progress for HUDs pick VersePickResult & { id } a pick completed (also delivered via the pick() promise) environment { name } lighting environment swapped view {} viewer entered the viewport (50 % visible) dwell { ms } cumulative on-screen time, emitted when the viewer scrolls away interact {} first user interaction (conversion signal) error { message } engine or load failure degraded { tier?, reason? } tier downgrade: WebGL2 fallback, or reason: "iframe-unavailable" when the frame never reported (poster stays) signed { name, signed } streamed scenes, after loaded: true = Ed25519 signature verified against this origin's /v1/pubkey; false = unsigned or altered; "unverified" = this browser could not check. Never blocks loading prop { id, count } a prop was spawned or thrown (id: -1 — scene cannot draw props) experience { name, props, hotspots: [{ id, label }] } an experience manifest was parsed; props load next hotspot { id, label?, title?, index? } the viewer jumped to a hotspot (goTo or the host's own UI) or, 2.7, opened a pin's card (label/title/index set then) hotspots { count, tour } 2.7: the authored layer mounted — pins on screen and guided-tour steps available (0 = no "Play tour") tour-step { step, of, hotspot } 2.7: the guided tour reached a step (hotspot is its pin id or null) stage { kind, walk, view, variants, version, lights, ar } the scene's staging manifest arrived: variants lists the configurator's variant names (2.5), version the scene version being served, lights the detected punctual light and emissive material names (2.7); ar (2.7) which AR path this device has for the scene — "webxr", "quicklook" or null (not product-scale, or no AR here) ar { mode, state, scale?, reason? } (2.8) a backdrop was applied — bg is the spec in effect; reload: true when a gradient, picture or transparent was asked for on an opaque canvas media { media?, audio?, surfaces?, material?, playing?, visible?, error? } a saveStill finished (2.7); the bytes ride the promise configuration { selection, cfg, total, priced, currency, skus, groups, ok? } Configurator depth (2.7): the owner's schema loaded, or the pick changed (setConfiguration, ?cfg=, the panel). ok false = a setConfiguration named an unknown group/option tour { name?, seconds? }] } live-tour roster changed — feed it to your own roster UI and follow(id); 2.7 peers carry flags (presenter, hand, muted, voice, laser) when set room { room, state, … } 2.7: joined (id), left, voice / voice-failed (message), presenter (presenter id or null, me, name), control (you took control from the presenter), action (a presenter action was applied here: action, detail, from), notice (voice cap reached, no direct connection to a peer) peer { room, id, name?, state, flags } 2.7: a peer joined, leaved, updated its flags (mute, presenting, hand) or raised a hand speaking { room, id, speaking, me } 2.7 voice: a peer (or this viewer, me) started / stopped speaking — detected locally on the received audio export-progress { id, percent, frame, total } video export progress, per captured frame export-done { id, size, cancelled, error? } export summary (the bytes ride the exportVideo() promise) review-posted { id, pos, text } client review (review: true only): a new pin was posted review-selected { id, pos, text } client review: an existing pin was opened measure VerseMeasureEvent inspection (2.7): a measure-tool tap (complete: false) or a finished measurement (id, mode, points, value, units, label) clip { count } inspection (2.7): the clip-plane set changed — count live planes objects { count, source, storeys, types } (2.7) the scene's IFC/USD object index loaded select { object, origin } (2.7) an object was selected — by a click (origin: "pick"), select() ("api") or ?select= ("link"); object null = cleared. pick events carry object too visibility { hidden } (2.7) objects were hidden or shown; how many are hidden now Copy viewer .on("ready", (d) => hud.tier.textContent = d.tier) .on("progress", (p) => hud.bar.style.width = `${(100 * p.drawn) / p.total}%`) .on("dwell", (d) => analytics.track("3d-dwell", { ms: d.ms })) .on("signed", (s) => badge.hidden = s.signed !== true) .on("error", (e) => console.warn("verse:", e.message)); VersePickResult# Field Type Meaning hit boolean false when the pick landed on sky / outside geometry position [x, y, z] world-space position of the picked surface point material number material index in the scene's material table cluster number internal cluster id (stable within one .vpk build) normal [x, y, z] | null the hit triangle's world-space normal, facing the viewer (2.7); null on a miss Client review pins in embeds# Client review is available inside the embed SDK, default off. Set review: true (or data-review="1" on the auto-mount script tag) and a viewer gets the exact same "click a spot, leave a note" workflow the playground has — rendered inside the iframe, over your scene, no playground chrome involved: A viewer toggles review mode with viewer.setReviewMode(true) (there is no built-in chip/button in the embed — that is the host page's UI to build, same as walk mode). While on, a clean click/tap does a GPU pick and opens a small composer at that spot; posting pins a numbered marker and fires review-posted. Existing pins render as the same numbered DOM markers the playground uses, projected from the camera pose each frame; clicking one opens its detail popover and fires review-selected. The composer/detail popover clamps to the iframe's own bounds and scrolls internally if it would overflow — it fits down to a 320px-wide embed. viewer.getComments() reads the current list without opening the UI — handy for a host-side counter/list. Auth: embed comments are anonymous by default — only the optional free-text "your name" field identifies an author, there is no signed-in viewer concept in an embed. A private scene needs the same share token as loading the scene itself; pass it once and both the scene bytes and the review reads/posts use it: Copy const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { vpk: "ingest/scene.vpk", share: "a1b2…32 hex chars…", review: true, }); viewer.on("ready", () => viewer.setReviewMode(true)); viewer.on("review-posted", (d) => console.log("new pin", d.id, d.pos, d.text)); Not in embeds: owner moderation (resolve/delete, the "show resolved" toggle's underlying data, the open/total counts on /v1/account/scenes) stays playground/studio-only — an embed viewer, even the scene's own owner browsing their own page, only ever sees the anonymous composer. Moderate from the playground or studio instead. See the parity table in api.md. TypeScript# Copy import type { VerseViewer, VerseEventMap } from "./verse-embed"; declare const viewer: VerseViewer; viewer.on("loaded", (d) => d.clusters); // d: VerseEventMap["loaded"] verse-embed.d.ts declares window.Verse: VerseGlobal (embed() and the optional auto-mounted instance). Copy it into your project or reference it from the Verse origin. Ingest from JavaScript# Uploading is a separate, tiny module — verse-sdk.js wraps POST /v1/ingest and the job polling, then mounts the result: Copy import { VerseClient } from "https://HOST/verse-sdk.js"; const verse = new VerseClient({ endpoint: "https://HOST", apiKey: "vk_…" }); const { url } = await verse.ingest(glbArrayBuffer, { name: "chair" }); verse.mount(document.querySelector("#viewer"), url); Protocol details: Ingest API.
